Chapter 3

Operating the Sequencer

#3.1 The controls

  • The named buttons each have their own job, and double as modifiers when held with another control. A held combination is written Shift + Play.
  • The four side buttons left of the pads launch the active track's clips in Track View, and whole scenes in Session View.
  • Left / Right (the arrows) page through a clip; + / − shift the pads' octave (on a drum track, the lane bank; in Session View, the rows).
  • Every gesture is listed in the Quick Reference.

#3.2 Transport

Play starts and stops the sequencer.

  • Shift + Play restarts from the top.
  • Loop + Play (Track View) restarts with the current clip at the page you're looking at.
  • Mute + Play turns the metronome on and off.
  • Delete + Play stops every clip while playing; while stopped it sends a MIDI panic.

dAVEBOx runs on its own clock by default; it can instead lock to Move's transport or send clock to external gear — see Routing & Sync.

#3.3 Switching views

Each view opens on its overview — its home screen, with the track row and the header naming the bank or mixer page.

  • On either view's overview, tap Note/Session to switch between Track View and Session View; hold it to peek at the other view.
  • Anywhere else — a bank page, menu, the sound editor, a dialog, a picker — Note/Session closes everything and takes you to Session View in one press, however deep you are.
  • Back steps out one level at a time; hold Back to go straight back to the overview of the view you're in.

#3.4 Reading the screen

The Track View overview, top to bottom:

  • Header: the bank the knobs are on, and at the right what the track plays — [MV1] Move instrument 1, [CH3] MIDI channel 3, [TR2] track 2's instrument, [CNDT] the Conductor, [--] nothing loaded, or a Schwung instrument's short name.
  • Under it: the key and scale (on a drum track, the lane bank and the selected lane's note), and the track's input velocity — VEL:LIVE follows how hard you play.
  • Track numbers: a box marks the active track; a muted track's number blinks, a soloed one is filled in.
  • Clip letters: under each track, the clip it's on (A–P), filled while it plays or is about to.
  • Page bar: one segment per page of the clip's loop — solid for the page you're viewing, outlined for the page playing, with a tick for the playhead. A small mark at either end means there are notes outside the loop.
  • Footer: what the controls do here — HLD BANKS (hold the jog for the bank map), TCH EDIT (touch a knob or the jog to see the bank's page and edit it) and SHFT TRK (Shift picks the track). Hold Shift and it reads JOG TRACK: turn the jog to change track. In Session View the footer is HLD BANKS TCH MIX (touch a knob or the jog for the mixer page). A bank page says HLD BANKS too while no knob is touched.

#3.5 Selecting a track

There are no dedicated track buttons. Change the active track with:

GestureWorks in
Shift + jog turnBoth views
Hold the jog and press Step 1–8 on the bank map (each lit in its track's colour; the track you're on blinks)Track View
Tap a clip pad (it also launches or stops that clip), or Shift + pad to open the clip in Track ViewSession View

#3.6 Parameter banks

Video

Tutorial 1.3: The bank map (from 2:40)

In Track View, the eight knobs control a bank of parameters, and the bank map — hold the jog — picks which bank. Each track has its own banks, in this order:

TrackBanks, in order
MelodicIN: PAD MODE → LIVE ARP · CTRL: MACROS · SEQ: STEP → CLIP · FX: NOTE FX → HARMONY → DELAY → SEQ ARP · MIX
DrumIN: RPT GROOVE · CTRL: MACROS · SEQ: STEP → ALL LANES → DRUM LANE · FX (the selected lane's): NOTE FX → DELAY · MIX
AudioIN: LIVE ARP · CTRL: MACROS · SEQ: CLIP → INPUT · FX: REMIX · MIX
SlicerIN: PAD MODE → LIVE ARP · CTRL: MACROS · SEQ: STEP → CLIP · FX: REMIX → NOTE FX · MIX
ConductorCLIP → STEP → NOTE FX · RSPD: ON/OFF → OCTAVE → TIMING

A melodic track starts on CLIP and a drum track on DRUM LANE: the banks before it are what plays into the track, the ones after it its effects (in the order the notes pass through them) and, last, MIX. CONFIG (the track's TRACK CONFIG menu) and AUTOMATION are reached from the bank map (below). They are screens, not banks: opening one never changes the bank you're on (the overview and a knob peek still show it), and Back from the screen's top level returns you exactly where you were. Shift + hold Step 11 jumps straight to LIVE ARP. The banks are grouped: IN (what you play in), CTRL (what moves the parameters), SEQ (the sequence) and FX (the note effects — on a drum track they apply to the selected lane). A Conductor starts on CLIP; its RSPD group is how the other tracks respond.

The banks are covered where they belong: Clip Timing & Grid, Sequencer Effects, STEP, CONFIG, MIX and MACROS, and AUTOMATION.

  • Hold the jog for the bank map: it appears the moment you press. The left 4×4 pads become a map of the track's banks and the screen shows the same map. Tap a pad to land on that bank — as many as you like, the map stays while you hold — and let go to play again. Letting go without tapping changes nothing. The map is up only while the jog is down; a click leaves nothing on screen.
  • Steps 1–8 are the tracks while the map is up (Track View), each lit in its track colour, with the track you are on blinking between its colour and white. Press one to switch track — the screen flashes TRACK n and what that track plays. The map stays up, now showing the new track's banks, so the bank you want there is the next tap. Steps 9–16 are dark and do nothing. Session View's map leaves the steps alone.
  • The right-hand pads open the track's module editors while the map is up (Track View): MIDI FX (cyan) above INSTRUMENT (the track's colour) in the third column, FX 1–4 (orange) down the far-right column. Tap one and the screen flashes its name and what is loaded there (or Empty); like CONFIG, it turns white and opens when you let go of the jog. Back from that editor takes you back to where you were. A MIDI track has only MIDI FX, and a Conductor none.
  • CONFIG, AUTOMATION and INST (and Session View's MASTER, SEND A and SEND B) open a screen, so they wait: the pad turns white, and the screen opens when you let go of the jog. Tap a bank after one and nothing opens.
  • From inside a screen — a menu, TRACK CONFIG, a module's editor, the AUTOMATION screen — hold the jog for about a third of a second and the same map comes up over it. Tap a pad and you leave the screen for that bank; let go without tapping and the screen is exactly as you left it. A quick click there is still a click (it lands as you let go). This works inside Move's own editor for a Move instrument too: the map shows over Move's screen, and Move's editor is back untouched when you let go. The map does not come up over the on-screen keyboard, over a question that needs an answer, or while Shift, Delete, Copy, Mute or Loop is held.
  • Turning the jog does not change the bank. On a bank with pages — MIX (the levels, then the channel strip), an Audio clip's SAMPLE and a Slicer's SLICER editor — it flips the pages (the header says which: 1/2, 2/3), and Delete + jog click resets only the page showing.
  • Touch the jog to see the current bank's page while your finger rests on it; let go and the overview is back. (In Session View it shows the mixer page.)
  • Touch a knob to see the bank's page while you touch it — nothing holds a bank page on screen by itself. Card Hold in Project Settings keeps it up for half a second, one or two after you let go, so you can read what you set. (Pages you open on purpose — Shift + hold Step 11's LIVE ARP page, the editors, AUTOMATION, TRACK CONFIG — stay until Back.)
  • Touch a knob and click the jog to switch a knob marked Alt in the bank tables to its alternate (Res → Zoom, Shift → Nudge, Dir → Reverse Style, Rand → Algo, Rate → Clock Feedback). Only that knob changes. Its cell has corner brackets, like the touch + click actions (Crop, Legato). While you touch it, the bottom of the screen shows CLK and the name it will switch to. Touch + click again, or Back, switches it back; leaving the bank does too. Touch + click also opens a bank's editors: Steps (knob 5) on SEQ ARP and LIVE ARP opens Arp Steps, any knob on RPT GROOVE switches between its Velocity and Nudge pages, and a knob on MACROS opens that macro. Delete + click on AUTOMATION clears the lane under the cursor. Each column of the map is a group, and its banks run top to bottom. A bank the track doesn't have leaves its pad dark, and nothing moves, so a bank is always on the same pad: | | IN | CTRL | SEQ | FX | |---|---|---|---|---| | Melodic | PAD MODE, LIVE ARP, —, CONFIG | MACROS, AUTO, —, MIX | STEP, CLIP, —, INST | NOTE FX, HARMONY, DELAY, SEQ ARP | | Drum | —, RPT GROOVE, —, CONFIG | MACROS, AUTO, —, MIX | STEP, DRUM LANE, ALL LANES, INST | NOTE FX, —, DELAY | | Audio | —, LIVE ARP, —, CONFIG | MACROS, AUTO, —, MIX | —, CLIP, INPUT, SAMPLE | —, —, REMIX | | Slicer | PAD MODE, LIVE ARP, —, CONFIG | MACROS, AUTO, —, MIX | STEP, CLIP, —, SLICER | NOTE FX, —, REMIX | | Conductor | —, —, —, CONFIG | ON/OFF, OCTAVE, TIMING (RSPD) | CLIP, STEP | NOTE FX | On a drum track the screen's map draws DRUM LANE and ALL LANES as one box: two views of the same lanes. The pads wear their group's color; the bank you're on is white, and CONFIG, MIX and INST wear the track's color. CONFIG and AUTOMATION open their menus (TRACK CONFIG, the AUTOMATION menu) when you let go of the jog; Back steps out. INST (beside MIX) is not a bank: it opens the track's instrument, and Back returns you to where you were. A Conductor has no INST.
  • Shift + jog steps through the tracks.
  • Each track remembers its bank, MIX and MACROS included — across track switches, suspend, and quit and relaunch.
  • Turning a knob that sets a number (an octave, an offset, a rate, a length, a count) turns its cell into an arc while you touch it, so the value moves the way the knob does. A knob with named choices (arp style, direction) opens its list instead, over a dimmed copy of the page.
  • Every bank lights its knob rings: knobs 1–4 white, 5–8 amber, brightness following the value. A dark ring means nothing is on that knob here. The Conductor's ON/OFF, OCTAVE and TIMING banks light each knob in its track's color.

Resetting a bank:

GestureResult
Delete + jog clickReset every parameter in the active bank (not ALL LANES, STEP, or the Conductor's ON/OFF, OCTAVE and TIMING). One-shot actions (Stretch, Shift, Legato, Crop) are left alone. On a drum track's RPT GROOVE bank, or any bank while Note Repeat is on, it resets the selected lane's groove
Delete + jog click on MACROSUnassign all eight macros on the track (asks first). Values and automation are left alone
Shift + Delete + jog clickReset all the sequencer effects — NOTE FX, HARMONY, DELAY and SEQ ARP. The CLIP, lane, STEP, MACROS and MIX banks, and automation, are left alone
Shift + Delete + side buttonReset the whole clip — notes and all parameters
  • Resets are undoable: Undo takes back a bank reset or a macro clear; Shift + Undo re-applies it.
  • Resetting a parameter also clears its automation. A bank reset clears the automation for that bank's parameters only; clearing or resetting a clip clears all of its automation. On a drum track, clearing a single lane leaves automation alone — a drum clip's automation covers the whole clip.

In Session View the knobs are the mixer, and the jog's map is the Session map:

  • Hold the jog: the MIXER column is Volume, Pan, Send A and Send B; the second column is the channel strip, EQ over COMPRESS; the fourth column, after a gap, is the FX column. It opens the Master, Send A and Send B effects directly, each level with its mixer row. The sends share a color.
  • On EQ, the knobs set one band on every track at once: Low first, and turning the jog steps through Mid, Mid Freq and High. The EQ pad reopens the band you were last on. Touch or turn a knob to see that track's EQ curve over the page. On COMPRESS, each knob is a track's comp, with the dot showing how hard it is working. As on a track, the map stays up while you hold the jog; the FX pads open their effects when you let go. The indicator at the top right names the mixer mode.
  • Touch a knob (or the jog) to see the mixer page. On the Send A or Send B page, touch a track's send and click to open that send's effects.
  • Mixer knobs record automation like any other: turn one while recording and it records into that track's clip.
  • A track that plays another track's instrument has no strip; its column shows a cross.
  • On a MIDI track, Volume is CC 7 and Pan is CC 10.

#3.7 Menus & Project Settings

Shift + Step 2 opens Project Settings — the settings saved with the project (except Card Hold, Monitor, Input, Input Gain, Bluetooth, Host Settings... and Move Settings..., which apply to every project). The full list is in Settings & Projects; many settings have a Shift + Step shortcut (see the Quick Reference).

Every list in dAVEBOx works the same way:

  • Turn the jog to move; the selected row is filled white, and a scrollbar shows when there's more.
  • A > at the right of a row opens something.
  • To change a number, click the row, turn the jog — the value shows in [brackets] while you change it — and click again to set it. A row with a list of choices opens the list: turn to one and click to set it, or press Back to leave it as it was. A two-way setting flips on the click.
  • Back steps out; in Project Settings it also cancels a change in progress.

#3.8 Choosing a track's sound

Video

Tutorial 1.5: Instruments (from 5:08) · Tutorial 1.6: Adding effects (from 6:14)

Each track's sound is set in its own menu, TRACK CONFIG:

  1. Hold the jog, tap the CONFIG pad (bottom-left of the bank map) and let go.
  2. The menu opens on Instmt/Dest, just below MIDI FX. Shift + click it to choose what the track plays: one of Move's four instruments, a Schwung instrument, a MIDI channel, and more.
  3. Click Instmt/Dest to edit the instrument. On a Move track this opens Move's own editor for it — change the kit or preset there as you would on Move, then press Back at the top of Move's editor to come back (Note/Session goes to Session View).
  4. Click an empty FX row to add an audio effect after the instrument.
  5. Click the empty MIDI FX row to add a MIDI effect in front of the instrument — on Move and MIDI tracks too.

A module picked from this menu loads and leaves you on the menu, on its row; click the row to edit it.

The right-hand pads of the bank map open these editors directly: MIDI FX, INSTRUMENT and FX 1–4. On an empty one the pad opens the module list, and the module you pick opens in its editor. While one is open, the map marks it (the instrument also lights INST) rather than the bank underneath.

Everything else in the menu is in Sound & Track Config.

#3.9 Saving, suspending & exiting

Video

Tutorial 7.1: Projects and Save state

dAVEBOx saves as you go — when you stop the transport, a moment after your last edit while stopped, at the end of a recording, and whenever you suspend, quit or switch projects. It never saves during playback, and there's no manual save. For named backups, use Save state.

A project has a size limit (about 1 MB — far more than most projects use). Past it, dAVEBOx shows PROJECT TOO BIG / SAVES ON QUIT ONLY / REMOVE SOME CLIPS and stops saving as you go — your work is still written in full when you quit or suspend; remove some clips and it saves as you go again, showing PROJECT SAVED. If a save cannot be written (storage full), it shows SAVE FAILED / CHECK STORAGE and tries again.

ActionResult
Shift + BackSave and hand the device back to official Schwung, from anywhere
Project Settings → QuitThe same
Project Settings → Suspend sessionPark dAVEBOx — it keeps playing in the background while you use Move
Power buttonPOWER OFF? — save everything and turn the Move off (tap or hold)
RebootReturns to official Schwung — unless you made dAVEBOx your boot default
  • Each asks first, opening on No — turn to Yes and click.
  • Power off saves your project, its instruments and effects, and the Move set, shows Powering off..., and turns the Move off. Press the power button to start it again as usual. Holding the button asks too — it never skips the question.
  • Leaving — or a reboot, even after a power cut mid-session — brings back your official install, your own Move sets included.
  • Suspend keeps dAVEBOx running in the background. To come back, hold Shift and hold Step 13 for half a second (or press Shift + Step 13 twice quickly), or pick dAVEBOx SA in the Tools menu — everything is as you left it.
  • If dAVEBOx is your boot default, hold Back at power-on and pick Schwung to go back.
PreviousQuick StartNext4. Tracks
Chapter 4

Tracks

dAVEBOx has 8 tracks. Each holds 16 clips, plays one clip at a time, and points at one instrument (see Choosing an instrument).

#4.1 Track type

A track's type sets how you enter notes into it and how it sequences them.

TypeWhere you set itHow it works
MelodicMode → MelodicScale-snapped notes on the pads and steps — Melodic Clips
DrumMode → Drums32 drum lanes, each its own step sequence — Drum Clips
AudioInstmt/Dest → AudioA sample per clip, played with the clip — Audio
SlicerInstmt/Dest → SlicerOne sample, chopped, the clips sequences of slices — Audio
ConductorInstmt/Dest → ConductorPlays no notes of its own; transposes the other tracks — The Conductor
  • Melodic and Drums are the Mode row of the track's TRACK CONFIG menu. Scrolling previews the type; clicking commits it.
  • Audio, Slicer and Conductor are chosen in the Instmt/Dest picker instead (Shift + click the row), just after the Move instruments. To turn one back into an ordinary track, choose an instrument in the same picker.
  • Tracks start Melodic, except Track 1 of a new project, which starts as a Drum track. A project started from your template keeps the template's track types.
  • A track keeps its color, clips and routing whatever its type — even as a Conductor, so its instrument is still there when you switch back.

#4.2 Changing type

Stop the transport first — tracks can't change type while playing. Changing type keeps your notes across all 16 clips (position, pitch, length and velocity) and resets the sequencer effects (NOTE FX, HARMONY, DELAY, SEQ ARP).

  • Melodic → Drum asks you to confirm if the track holds notes. Each pitch becomes its own lane (a clip with more than 32 pitches loses the least-used ones), and per-step conditions are dropped.
  • Drum → Melodic doesn't ask. The lanes merge into one clip with the length of the first lane that has notes, and per-step conditions are dropped.
  • Making a Conductor always asks (Make Conductor?). It keeps the notes and their conditions, and clears effects, arps and automation. Only one track can be the Conductor; trying on a second track says which track already is. Choosing an instrument turns a Conductor back into a melodic track, without asking.
  • Choosing Audio or Slicer clears the track's notes (they were pitches, and on a Slicer a pitch is a slice), asking first if there are any. The track's instrument goes and its effects stay; it plays through the track's own Schwung slot — a Move track takes one.
  • Choosing Audio on a track that plays an instrument and has clips first asks Resample the clips? Yes records each clip with notes, one after another and each alone, then converts: every clip becomes an Audio clip playing its own recording. The instrument is recorded before its effects, which stay on the track, so it sounds the same. For a Move instrument (or a track that plays another track's instrument) those are the effects on its Move track's FX 1–4: they're copied onto the Audio track with its volume, pan and sends, and the original stays where it was. The recordings go straight into the project. Back while it records cancels the whole change. No converts without recording (the notes are cleared). Back on the question changes nothing. Flatten track does the same from TRACK CONFIG, and lets you record the effects too.
  • Leaving Audio or Slicer (choosing an instrument, or the other of the two) clears every clip's steps and lets go of the samples, asking first; one Undo brings it all back. The files stay in the project until you purge them.
Previous3. Operating the SequencerNext5. Track View
Chapter 5

Track View

Track View is where you build one clip, always the active track's current clip:

  • The pads play the track's notes (melodic) or trigger its drum lanes.
  • The 16 step buttons hold the clip's pattern.
  • Hold the jog for the bank map: tap a pad to choose the bank that shapes the clip.

Clip contents are covered in Melodic Clips and Drum Clips.

#5.1 Switching clips

The four side buttons (left of the pads) launch the active track's clips. They follow the four clip rows shown in Session View; the lit button is the clip you're editing.

GestureResult
Side buttonSelect and launch that clip
Side button of the playing clipStop it at the end of its page (again to cancel)
Shift + top / bottom side buttonScroll the four visible clips up / down one (the same window for every track)
Copy + side button, then anotherCopy the clip to that slot (Shift + Copy cuts)
Delete + side buttonClear its notes and automation (and free its length for the next recording)
Shift + Delete + side buttonReset it — notes and all parameters

#5.2 Muting the track

  • Mute silences the active track; Shift + Mute solos it.
  • Delete + Mute clears every mute and solo (on a drum track, just its lane mutes and solos).
  • A live pad you hold still plays through a muted track.
  • In Session View you mute each track from its knob — see Arranging.
Previous4. TracksNext6. Melodic Clips
Chapter 6

Melodic Clips

A melodic clip is a sequence of scale-snapped notes on a step grid. The Sequencer Effects and Automation that shape it have their own chapters.

#6.1 Playing and placing notes

Video

Tutorial 3.1: Placing notes

The pads play notes from the current key and scale. + / − shifts the pad octave; a new track's pads start one octave up.

While you hold notes (pads or an external keyboard), the screen names them in brackets at the right of the key/scale row — the note ([F#3]) or the chord:

  • Middle C is C3, as on Move.
  • A raised dot after a chord name ([A♭MAJ7˙]) means the chord is played without its third.
  • A combination with no common name shows its notes instead ([C C# D]).
  • Flat keys spell with flats, the key label included (B♭ MINOR).
  • Only what you play is shown, never the sequencer's notes.

To place notes on the grid, use the 16 step buttons:

ActionResult
Tap an empty stepPlaces the last note you played, at velocity 100 (or the track's fixed VelIn). With nothing played yet, the screen says NO NOTE
Tap a filled stepClears it
Hold a stepThe knobs on screen now act on that step (see Editing notes). An empty step stays empty until you press a pad while holding it
Press several steps at onceEach empty step gets the last note. On a melodic track, a filled step after the first is silenced but keeps its notes — do it again to bring them back. On a drum track, a filled step is cleared
Hold a step with notes, then tap a later stepStretch the note to reach it — see Editing notes
Hold a step, turn a knob to set a lock, then tap a later stepStretch the lock's value to reach it — see Editing notes
Copy + step → another stepCopy the step's notes (same clip); Shift + Copy cuts
Delete + stepClear the step, and any automation on it (a lock is a knob value set for one step — see Automation)

Steps past the clip's length are dimmed. These step gestures work on drum steps too — see Drum Clips.

#Pad layouts

Each melodic track has its own pad layout, whatever its instrument (Move, Schwung, MIDI). Choose it on the Pad Mode bank (the top pad of the IN column on the bank map): knob 1, Mode, picks the layout and the other knobs are that layout's own settings. Each layout keeps its settings when you switch to another and back. Shift + Step 8 also steps through the five layouts, and the screen flashes IN-SCALE, CHROMATIC, PIANO or CUSTOM CHORDS:

  • Scale (default) — only in-scale notes, with the root in the track color. Each row starts three scale notes above the row below.
  • Chrom — all 12 semitones, in-scale notes highlighted. Each row carries on from the end of the row below.
  • Piano — two keyboard octaves from C: the lower octave on the bottom two rows, the higher on the top two. Each octave's bottom row is the white keys (C to the next C) and the row above it the black keys, each sitting between its two white keys; pads with no black key are dark and silent. The root is in the track color and in-scale keys are brighter than the rest. On the Pad Mode bank, Oct A / Trans A move the bottom octave (zone A) and Oct B / Trans B the top one (zone B), each on its own. Instr switches the pads to Bass: four strings (E A D G from the bottom row up), the open string and seven frets across each, with one Oct and Trans for the whole neck. Piano and Bass each keep their own settings.
  • Chord — below.
  • Custom — chords you build yourself on the bottom row, the Scale layout on the other three. See The Custom layout.

A Conductor's pads have Scale and Chrom only, from Shift + Step 8; it has no Pad Mode bank.

Delete + jog click on the Pad Mode bank resets the current layout's settings. Mode and Piano's Instr stay as they are, and so do your Custom chords; Undo brings the settings back.

Splitting the pads (Scale and Chrom). On the Pad Mode bank:

  • Split — None, Vert (the left 4x4 and the right 4x4 are two separate note grids) or Horz (the bottom two rows and the top two). Zone A is always the left or bottom one, B the right or top one.
  • Oct A / Oct B — each zone's octave. With no split there is one Oct for the whole grid.
  • Trans A / Trans B — where each zone starts. In Scale it counts scale notes, so the pads stay in key (+2 in C major starts on E); in Chrom, semitones.
  • Zone B's pads show their colors the other way round — the root dim white, the other notes in the track color — so the two zones read apart.
  • Scale and Chrom share the split and the octaves; each keeps its own Transpose.

Octave buttons. + / − move the whole surface. Shift + + / − move only zone B: the B split, Piano's top octave, or the pads above the chords in Chord and Custom. Where there is no zone B (no split, Bass) Shift makes no difference.

#The Chord layout

Video

Tutorial 3.8: The Chord layout (from 8:52)

The Chord layout plays a whole chord from one pad, always in the track's key and scale. Switching to it with Shift + Step 8 puts the track on its Pad Mode bank.

  • Bottom row: eight chords — by default I ii iii IV V vi vii° and I an octave up (the Map knob regroups them) — colored by function (tonic, subdominant, dominant). They follow key and scale changes.
  • Row 2: hold 7, 9, sus2, sus4, add9 or 5 while you press a chord to change it, or press one while a chord is held to change it as it sounds. The last two pads, Inv− and Inv+, move the voicing down or up one note: hold one before a chord for that press, or tap it while a chord is held (each tap moves it further).
  • Row 3: the notes of the last chord you played, rising — strum or pick them. They stay after you let go.
  • Top row: the scale, with the key's root on the fourth pad — three notes below it, four above (G A B C D E F G in C major).
  • On the Pad Mode bank, after Mode, the Chord layout's knobs are:
    • Map — how the chords sit on the bottom row. Diatonic: I ii iii IV V vi vii° I. Function groups them by job: the home chords (I vi iii), the away chords (IV ii), the ones that pull home (V vii°), then I an octave up. A chord you have edited moves with its degree to its new pad.
    • Voicing — moves every chord at once.
    • Smooth — Off; Follow (each chord takes the voicing nearest the one you played last); Anchor (every chord takes the voicing nearest one chord you choose on the Anchor knob, which appears only in this mode).
    • Bass — Off, or the root added one (−1) or two (−2) octaves below.
    • Pad Oct — moves rows 3 and 4 (the pads above the chords) by octaves; Shift + + / − does the same.
    • Slots: Play / Select — in Select the chord pads are silent and only choose what row 3 strums.
  • To edit a chord, hold it while on the Pad Mode bank. The page switches to that chord, titled with its numeral and name (vi · AMIN) — Root, Stack, Inversion, Spread, Bass (Off / Root / 3rd / 5th) and Octave, plus Reset on knob 8 (touch it and click the jog) — and switches back when you let go.
    • On every other bank a held chord leaves the knobs alone, so you can play chords and turn sound or sequencer knobs at the same time.
    • A stack with no in-key version on that chord (sus4 on IV in a major key) plays the plain chord, and the page says so.
  • While you hold a chord, Track View names it with its numeral: [vi · AMIN]. Lowercase numerals are minor, ° is diminished.
  • Holding a step and tapping a chord writes the whole chord into the step.

#The Custom layout

The Custom layout gives you eight chords of your own on the bottom row. The other three rows are the Scale layout, starting from the root at the left of row 2. A chord keeps the exact notes you put in it; changing the key or scale does not change it. Chords are saved per track.

  • Play: press a chord pad. A pad with a chord is cyan, so the row stands apart from the note pads; an empty one is dark and silent. Track View names the held chord ([CMAJ7]).
  • Build or edit: hold a chord pad and tap pads on the upper rows. Each tap adds that note, or removes it if the chord already has it. A chord holds up to six notes.
    • While you hold a chord, its notes are lit white on the upper rows.
    • Each pad you tap sounds as you tap it. A chord that is already sounding changes as you edit it.
    • An empty chord stays silent while you fill it; you hear the whole chord the next time you press its pad.
    • Notes added this way are not written into a recording in progress.
  • Or notes first: hold the notes on the upper rows and tap an empty chord pad — it takes them (the lowest six). A pad that already has a chord just plays, so holding a note over the chords never changes one.
  • From a USB keyboard: both work with keys too. Hold a chord pad and play keys, or hold keys and tap an empty chord pad. Keys behave just like the pads: each one adds or removes a note, they sound as you play them, and they are not recorded or captured. The keyboard must be on dAVEBOx's MIDI-in channel.
  • Copy a chord: hold Copy, tap the chord, then tap each pad that should get it. Shift + Copy moves it instead. Undo takes back the last paste.
  • Octaves: + / − move the whole surface (OCTAVE); Shift + + / − move only the upper rows (PAD OCTAVE), to reach notes in another octave while building a chord.
  • Move one chord an octave: hold its pad and press + or − (Hold: Assign only).
  • Clear a chord: Delete + its pad. Undo brings it back.
  • Holding a step and tapping a chord writes the whole chord into the step.

On the Pad Mode bank (Custom):

  • Hold — Assign (default): holding a chord pad edits it, as above. Play: holding a chord pad just plays it, so you can play the scale pads with it and nothing is added; holding notes never fills an empty pad either.
  • Chd Oct — the chord row's octave. Pad Oct — the upper rows' octave. These are the same two the Octave buttons move.
  • Trans — where the upper rows start, counted in scale notes (they stay in key).
  • Build a chord by name: hold a chord pad while on the Pad Mode bank and the page becomes its card — the same knobs as the Chord layout's card, titled with the chord: Root (any note), Stack (Maj, Min, Dim, Aug, Sus2, Sus4, 7, Maj7, Min7, m7b5, Dim7, 6, Min6, Add9, 9, Maj9, Min9, 7sus4, 5), Inv, Sprd (Open lifts the second-lowest note an octave), Bass (Off / Root / 3rd / 5th), Oct and Reset (touch knob 8 and click the jog: the pad empties). The card starts from the chord the pad already holds; a turn replaces its notes with the chord on the card. One Undo brings back what the pad held before you picked it up. It works in Assign and in Play.

#6.2 Several notes on one step

A step holds up to eight notes. Build a chord two ways:

  • Pads first: hold one or more pads, then press a step.
  • Step first: hold a step, then tap pads one at a time. Tap a held note again to remove it.

#6.3 Editing notes

Video

Tutorial 3.2: Editing a step (from 1:02)

Holding a step points whatever knobs are on screen at that step:

  • On the STEP bank (on the bank map, the top pad of the SEQ column, above CLIP) the knobs are the note's own settings, listed below. With no step held the bank reads Hold step to edit.
  • On a module editor, MACROS, or a sequencer-effect bank (NOTE FX, HARMONY, DELAY, SEQ ARP, and CLIP's Dir), the knobs write a lock at that step (see Automation).
  • LIVE ARP and the rest of CLIP do nothing under a held step.

Reach the note settings from anywhere: hold a step with notes and turn the jog right to show its STEP page; turn left (or let go) to return. A JOG RIGHT / Edit step card appears as the hold begins; the footer reads JOG STEP while holding and JOG BACK on the step page. Empty steps have no step page.

  • Edits apply to every note in the step, and one hold is one undo.
  • Stretch a note: once the hold has begun (the Edit step card shows), tap a later step to set the note's length up to it; tap that step again to shorten it by one. Left / Right still page, so a note can stretch past the current page. (Tapping steps together, without the pause, toggles them instead.)
  • Stretch a lock: if the last thing you did while holding the step was turn a knob to set a lock, tapping a later step stretches that lock's value up to and including it instead, the same as on the AUTOMATION screen: tap the end again to shorten it, or turn the knob again to change the whole range. While you hold, the range lights orange, not the note-length colour, so you can tell which one you're stretching. Only the parameter you turned last is stretched. Editing the note again (a STEP knob, a pad) puts the tap back to stretching the note.
  • A note nudged past half a step moves to the neighbouring step when you let go.
  • + / − moves the octave range to reach higher or lower notes.
KnobOn screenAdjusts
1NotePitch, by scale degree
2OctPitch, by octave
3LengNote length (gate)
4VelVelocity
5NudgTiming, up to ±1 step
6IterIteration (below)
7ProbProbability (below)
8RatchRatchet (below)

#Per-step conditions

Video

Tutorial 3.4: Steps that decide for themselves (from 4:21)

Three settings decide whether and how a step fires. Each is off by default — Iter and Ratch read --, Prob reads 100 %:

  • Iteration (Iter) plays the step only on certain passes of the loop: 2:3 plays on the 2nd pass of every three. The counter resets on a cold start (Stop → Play).
  • Probability (Prob) gives the step a chance of playing, from 100 % down to 1 %. The roll is per note, so chords thin out unevenly.
  • Ratchet (Ratch) retriggers the step 2, 3 or 4 times within its slot.

They stack in that order: iteration decides if the step plays, probability rolls per note, and a note that plays fires all its ratchets.

The conditions belong to the step's notes: removing the step's last note (tap its pad while holding the step) clears them, as clearing the step does.

#6.4 Recording

Video

Tutorial 3.5: Recording (from 5:40)

Press Record to play notes into the active clip in real time.

TransportWhat happens
StoppedA 1-bar count-in, then recording and playback start together
PlayingRecords immediately, from wherever the playhead is
  • While playing, Record is a punch: press to drop in, again to drop out, both taking effect the moment you press.
  • A take that began with the count-in into an empty clip keeps going — the clip grows a page at a time for as long as you play. Press Record to finish: the clip keeps the page the playhead is in, so press it in the last page you want.
  • Recording adds to what's there and never erases. For a clean take, clear the clip first (Delete + side button); that also frees its length so the take sizes itself to what you play.
  • Notes played in the last half-beat of the count-in land on step 1.
  • You can switch tracks mid-take; recording follows the active track.
  • Recording needs the Forward playback direction. A clip set to another direction shows REC UNAVAILABLE: set its Dir to Fwd, or choose Bake Now (see Bake).

#Step recording

Video

Tutorial 3.7: Step recording (from 8:03)

With the transport stopped on a melodic track, Shift + Record opens step entry (drum and Conductor tracks don't have it). Record turns white and one step blinks white — the cursor, starting at the first step of the page you're viewing.

  • Play a pad (or several together for a chord): the notes land on the cursor step, and the cursor moves on when you let go.
  • Right with pads held ties the note a step longer, each press extending it; Left with pads held takes one step back off. The steps the note is held over light in the tail colour as you go, as they do when you hold a step.
  • Right alone is a rest: the cursor moves on, writing nothing.
  • Left steps back and erases what you entered there this session. Notes already in the clip stay.
  • The cursor stops at the clip's last step; it never wraps.

Leave with Shift + Record, Record, Back, or press Play to hear it. One undo takes back the whole step-recording session.

Note

Live Merge is unavailable while step entry is open — leave it first.

#6.5 Capture

Video

Tutorial 3.6: Capture (from 6:33)

dAVEBOx is always listening: play something, then tap Capture to keep it.

  • Notes you play while not recording are held in a buffer; Capture writes them into the clip.
  • That includes notes from an external MIDI keyboard or controller.
  • With LIVE ARP on, what is kept is the arpeggio you heard, not the pads you held; with Note Repeat, each repeated hit — the same as recording.
  • With a MIDI effect set to Pre, what is kept is what the effect played (see Editing a module).
  • Knob moves are held too, and land as automation.
  • The Capture button blinks white while there's something to keep.
Like Move

this is Move's Capture — play first, keep it after.

What Capture does depends on the transport:

TransportWhat Capture does
PlayingAdds the buffered notes to the current clip where you played them; knob moves become automation. Into an empty clip, the take keeps the beat you played it on and starts on the next bar
Stopped, empty projectReads a tempo from your playing, sizes a clip to whole bars, and starts it
Stopped, current clip emptyFits the take to the current tempo; the Fit to bars screen lets the jog pick how many bars it fills (Shift + jog fine-stretches it)
Stopped, current clip holds notesSession View opens — tap a blinking empty clip on that track to keep the take (Record cancels)
  • After a stopped capture into an empty project, a tempo chooser offers the detected BPM and nearby candidates over a strip of your take against the bars. Playback keeps rolling as you scroll them.
  • Capture works on drum clips too.
  • One Undo takes back any capture.
  • Shift + Capture clears the buffer, knob moves included.

What the buffer holds — what you just played:

  • at most the last 8 bars;
  • playing over a spot you already played on an earlier lap replaces that lap, so four passes of jamming keep the last one;
  • it starts afresh when you select another track, edit a clip by hand (entering steps, clearing), launch a clip or scene, arm Record, start or stop the transport, or pause for about two bars;
  • every Capture tap empties it, even one that found nothing to keep.

Capturing knob moves:

  • Any parameter you turn while the loop runs with Record off is kept; one Capture tap commits them all into the clip you heard them in, as smooth, editable lanes.
  • Knob moves are only buffered while the transport runs. Another lap replaces what the last lap kept, and stopping clears them.

#6.6 Clip length & the loop

Video

Tutorial 3.9: Loop length and pages (from 10:10)

A clip plays its loop — a run of up to 256 steps, shown as pages of 16. The loop is the clip's length, and it normally starts on step 1.

  • Left / Right moves between the pages inside the loop. While the transport runs, this also pauses Seq Follow, so the page stays where you went; it follows again the next time the transport stops. (Restarting with Shift + Play or Loop + Play isn't a stop, so the pause stays.)
  • Seq Follow keeps the step display on the page that's playing. It is one switch for the whole device and is remembered between sessions: hold Left or Right and press Play to turn it on or off. That press does nothing else; the transport isn't started or stopped. It works in the sound editors too, but not in Session view. On the track overview, a small ▶| mark left of Vel: shows Follow is on. It blinks while an arrow has paused it, and it's gone when Follow is off.
  • Loop + jog grows or shrinks the loop by a step.
  • Shift + Step 15 doubles the loop and copies what's in it into the new half.

Hold Loop for the loop view: the step buttons stand for pages, and a page inside the loop lights in the track color (pulsing if it holds notes). While Loop is held:

GestureSets the loop to
Jog ±1Grow or shrink from the end
Tap a pageEnd the loop on that page (from page 1, or from the loop's start if it starts later)
Hold one page, tap anotherThe range between them

Notes outside the loop are kept and return when you widen it. For example, to make a 2-bar clip on the 1/16 grid, hold Loop and tap Step 2. Tap Step 2 again on a 2-page loop to go back to one page. While a take is recording, the loop length can't be changed.

Tap Loop instead of holding it and the loop view stays up (the Loop button blinks white) so you can set the loop with your hands free. The pads keep playing. Tap Loop again, or press Back, to close it; switching to Session View or opening a menu closes it too. A tap that already does something else still does only that: on a drum track with a latched repeat it releases the repeat, and with the arpeggiator's latch holding notes it clears them.

Copying pages. Hold Loop and Copy, tap a lit page (it blinks), then tap another page: it becomes an exact copy — every note, velocity, length and step setting; empty steps too. Keep holding Copy to paste onto more pages. Shift + Copy cuts. A paste past the end of the clip makes the clip longer, and one before the loop's start moves the start back. Only what plays is copied: steps outside the loop count as empty. Automation stays where it is. On a drum track it copies the selected lane, or every lane on the ALL LANES bank. One Undo takes a paste back.

The clip transforms — Stretch, Shift, Nudge, Legato and Zoom — need the loop to start on step 1; on a loop that starts later they do nothing and the screen says LOOP STARTS AFTER STEP 1 / CROP FIRST. Crop (CLIP knob 6: touch it and click the jog) makes the loop the whole clip: it moves to step 1 and everything outside it is removed. One Undo brings it back.

#6.7 Undo

Undo reverses the last edit; Shift + Undo redoes it. Undo is one step deep and covers step and clip edits, copy and clear, recording, bakes and more.

Previous5. Track ViewNext7. Drum Clips
Chapter 7

Drum Clips

On a drum track, each sound is a lane — its own step sequence with its own length, timing and effects. A track has 32 lanes, each mapped to a MIDI note that triggers one sound in the instrument.

The pad grid splits in two:

HalfHolds
Left 4×416 drum lanes. Tap one to hear its sound and select it — the steps then show that lane.
Right 4×4Velocity zones, or a note-repeat mode

The left pads show 16 lanes at a time; + / − switches between lane bank A and bank B. The screen shows the active bank.

The pads tell the DRUM LANE bank from the rest. On DRUM LANE the selected lane is the track's colour (dim if it has no hits), lanes with hits are light grey, empty lanes are dark grey, and the velocity pads are dim track colour. On every other bank — ALL LANES included — the selected lane is white, lanes with hits are the track's colour, and the velocity pads are grey. A muted lane is always off.

#7.1 Placing hits

Video

Tutorial 2.1: Lanes, hits and velocity

Select a lane, then tap steps 1–16 to add or clear its hits. The steps always show the selected lane.

Velocity zones (the right 4×4) set the velocity of the hits you place next — 16 zones from 8 (bottom-left) to 127 (top-right). A zone pad also plays the selected lane at that velocity; with a step held it sets that hit's velocity, or places the hit if the step was empty. While you hold a step with a hit, the zone nearest its velocity lights white.

A lane's sound is set by its MIDI note, on the NOTE FX bank: knob 1 moves it by an octave, knob 2 by a semitone. The screen shows the note, e.g. Pad: C1 (36). A new drum track's bank A plays notes 36–51 — the notes of a Move drum kit's 16 pads — so a Move kit lines up pad for pad.

Editing a hit works the same as note edit, minus the pitch knobs: Leng, Vel and Nudg on knobs 1–3, Iter, Prob and Ratch on 5–7. (On a drum hit, tapping the same step again doesn't shorten it.)

#7.2 Per-lane loops

Video

Tutorial 2.2: Euclidean rhythms and per-lane loops (from 1:39)

Each lane has its own loop length: Loop + jog on the selected lane. On the ALL LANES bank, Loop + jog and the loop-page gestures set every lane at once. Lanes of different lengths (kick 16, hat 12, percussion 10) make a polyrhythm from one clip.

As on a melodic clip, the transforms need a lane's loop to start on step 1 — on ALL LANES, every lane's. Crop moves it there: DRUM LANE knob 6 for the selected lane, ALL LANES knob 5 for every lane.

#7.3 Note Repeat

Video

Tutorial 2.3: Note Repeat (from 3:08)

Note Repeat retriggers a lane at a steady rate. Shift + Step 8 cycles the right pads between velocity zones and the two repeat modes; entering a repeat mode names it and puts the track on its RPT GROOVE bank. Opening a project puts the right pads back on velocity zones.

The bottom two rows of the right pads are rates (straight, then triplet); the top two rows are an 8-step gate mask — see the drum pad diagram.

  • Rpt1 repeats the selected lane: hold a rate pad. Velocity follows pad pressure, and you can change lanes while holding.
  • Rpt2 repeats any lane at a rate you assign it: tap a rate pad to assign it to the selected lane, then hold a lane pad. Hold several for layered repeats.

Latch keeps a repeat going after you let go:

  • Loop + rate pad (Rpt1) or Loop + lane pad (Rpt2) — or press Loop while already holding one.
  • Tap a latched pad again to release it.
  • Loop with no pads held, or Delete + Loop, releases every latch on the track. Stopping the transport clears them too.
  • Latched lanes light cyan.

The gate mask (top two rows) is a looping on/off pattern over the repeats:

  • All steps are on by default; tap to toggle.
  • Loop + a gate pad sets its cycle length (1–8) and turns every gate in it back on; gates past the cycle show dark grey.
  • Delete + a gate pad resets that step's groove.
  • Per-step velocity and timing are on the RPT GROOVE bank.

#7.4 Copying, clearing & muting lanes

  • Copy + lane pad, then tap another lane to paste (the destination keeps its own MIDI note). Shift + Copy cuts.
  • Mute + lane pad mutes a lane; Shift + Mute + lane pad solos it (the two cancel each other). Delete + Mute clears the track's lane mutes and solos.
  • Delete + lane pad clears the lane's hits (LANE CLEARED).
  • Shift + Delete + lane pad resets the lane — hits, length, loop, effects and repeat groove — but keeps its sound (LANE RESET).

#7.5 Audio

Two kinds of track play samples instead of sending notes — choose either in the track's Instmt/Dest picker:

KindWhat it is
AudioEach clip holds its own sample and plays it with the clip — set and forget, locked to the clip's playhead and kept in time with the project. For loops, stems, whole recordings.
SlicerOne sample for the whole track, cut into slices you play, sequence and rearrange from the pads. Every clip of the track plays the same slices: a clip is a step sequence of slices. For breaks, and for chopping up anything.

Both play through the track's own Schwung slot, so its effects, fader, pan, sends and mute apply. Nothing on either receives MIDI.

#Audio tracks

Each clip knows its sample's own Tempo (0.1–999.9 BPM) — guessed when you pick it: a tempo in the file's name ("84 bpm") is taken as it is, even with a tail after the loop; else bars in the name ("4bar"), else where its beats fall, else the project's tempo. Turn it if the guess is wrong. A new pick sets the clip to the sample's length in whole bars at that Tempo (up to 256 bars). The sample plays from Start each time the clip comes round, for the clip's own length. Warp (on SAMPLE's TIME page) says how it meets the project's tempo:

  • Warp (the default) time-stretches the loop and keeps its pitch — at any tempo it sounds as recorded, only faster or slower, and Pitch and Detune transpose it without changing its length. Warp is processor-intensive: one or two warped tracks are fine, but warping many at once can overload the Move and cause clicks or dropouts.
  • Vintage cuts the sample into tiny pieces on the sequencer's own clock (384 to a bar) and starts each on its place at the sample's Tempo, crossfading from one to the next — the same sound at its own tempo, and in time at any other, with the grit of an old sampler.
  • Pitch retunes the loop, faster or slower, to the tempo (Pitch and Detune then give way: the tempo sets the speed).

Vintage and Pitch cost almost nothing. Loop + steps sets the loop as on any clip: the clip plays the part of the sample under those steps, laid over it from Start at its Tempo — on the SAMPLE screen too.

The pads show where the loop is: the clip in 32 even sections, one a pad, dim in the track colour, the sections played this time round bright, the one playing pulsing. On a pass that plays backwards they fill from the end. Stopped, all dim. Sections past the end of the sample show grey — the clip never plays them. Tapping one does nothing. The steps show where the loop is too: dim, the playhead white, following it page by page while it plays. An Audio clip has no sequence, so no STEP, NOTE FX or PAD MODE bank.

#Slicer tracks

A Slicer holds one sample and its slices, the same for every clip. Its clips are sequences: each step holds one slice, placed and recorded as on any track — hold a step + tap a pad places that slice. One slice plays at a time: a new slice cuts the last — unless it's the next piece of the sample, reached right where the last one has got to, which simply plays on. Every slice plays at one level (velocity is ignored); for more voices or velocity, Convert to kit (below) and play it on a drum track. Chopping is what you do to a sample; a slice is a piece it makes.

Each step has its own sound. Hold a step: K2 Pitch (±24 semitones, on top of the slice's own), K3 Length — how much of its slice the step plays, 100 % being all of it — with Start behind it (touch K3 + click), where in the slice it begins, and K4 Dir: Slice (the step plays as its slice does), or the arrow forwards or backwards, whatever the slice says. So one slice can play whole on one step, just its tail backwards on the next, and an octave up on a third. A step left at 100 % / 0 % / Slice plays the slice as it is. These stay with the step through every edit, copy and Undo, a ratchet repeats them, and a pad played by hand always plays the slice as it is. REMIX's Revrs turns a step round whatever its Dir.

Loading a sample doesn't chop it: it is one slice, from Start to End, until you chop it (below). The steps you already have stay. A Slicer takes samples up to 4 minutes.

Start and End are the Slicer's range (page 3 of the SLICER editor). Slices play only inside it: a slice crossing Start or End plays just the part inside, and a slice wholly outside is silent, its pad dark grey — still there to pick, and it plays again as soon as the range covers it. Moving the range never moves or re-cuts the slices. Every way of making slices stays inside the range.

The pads are the slices, in time order, 32 to a page; a slice playing, or a pad held, is white. Pads past the slice count are dark. A Slicer holds up to 128 slices: Octave Up / Down shows the next or previous 32. They sit as PAD MODE says: 4 Rows (8 a row from the bottom-left) or 16 Pads (the left 4×4, then the right 4×4 — two banks, the right one in the colours of its partner track: 1 with 5, 2 with 6, 3 with 7, 4 with 8). From an external keyboard, note 36 plays slice 1.

A Slicer has its own Tempo (guessed when the sample loads, as an Audio clip's) and Sync: Off (the default) plays the slices at their own speed, as cut; Pitch retunes them, faster or slower, by the project's tempo against the sample's Tempo — a break follows the project as a sped-up or slowed-down record would; Warp stretches the whole sample to the project's tempo at its own pitch (offered for samples up to a minute; a tempo change re-stretches it in the background a moment later). A Slicer follows the Conductor as any track does, by the Conductor's RESPONDER bank — but it starts with its RESPONDER off (when it becomes a Slicer, or a Conductor is made): a break isn't usually something to move with the key.

#The SLICER editor

The SLICER editor is a Slicer's instrument: the bank map's SLICER pad (where INST is on other tracks), the right 4×4's instrument pad, the instrument row in the track's sound menu, or Shift + hold Note/Session. It has three pages — turn the jog for the next (the header reads 1/3, 2/3, 3/3). The pads pick the slice the knobs on pages 1 and 2 edit.

PageK1K2K3K4K5K6K7K8
1 SLICES — the waveformStartZoomEndPlayPitchDetuneRevrsGain
2 SHAPEAttkDecay
3 SAMPLE — the whole fileStartZoomEndSyncPitchDetuneTempoGain

Page 1, SLICES shows the waveform with the slices on it, the picked one bracketed, the audio outside the range dotted. K1 / K3 move the picked slice's start / end, one screen pixel a detent (a slice ends where the next begins, E NEXT; turn its end away to set its own). K2 zooms. K4–K8 are the slice's Play (One to its end, Gate as long as the step, Thru on to the range's End — the next slice cuts it off), Pitch, Detune, Revrs and Gain, each on top of the sample's. Delete + pad removes a slice (it joins the one before; slice 1 stays).

Click (the corner brackets say so) to enter the slice editor: the jog moves a cursor through the range and a click adds a slice there; everything else works as outside. Back leaves it.

Page 2, SHAPE: the slice's Attk and Decay. Decay falls away as a drum pad's does — quickly, then a long tail — and its knob is finest at the short end, 1 ms a detent.

Hold Shift on pages 1 and 2 and Play, Revrs, Attk and Decay set every slice at once (-- where they differ). Start, Zoom and End rest while Shift is held, their rings dark and their values off the screen. Pitch, Detune and Gain do nothing with Shift: page 3's are the sample's, and move every slice together while keeping each slice's own difference.

Page 3, SAMPLE is the whole file: a strip of the waveform over K1–K3 with the range marked on it, the audio outside it dotted. K1 / K3 move the range's Start / End (a strip pixel a detent, Shift a single sample); K2 zooms the strip round the edge you moved last (a magnifier marks it). Touch Start, Zoom, End or Gain and the waveform comes up large over the page while you hold the knob, the range and the slices on it. K4 Sync (above), K5 Pitch, K6 Detune, K7 Tempo (1 BPM a detent, Shift 0.1) and K8 Gain are the sample's: the base every slice adds its own to. Touch Tempo and click for Original tempo: the sample's Tempo becomes the project's.

The menus. Shift + click on pages 1 and 2 opens the SLICE menu (not from inside the slice editor, where a click adds a slice):

  • Load sample — the chooser (see SAMPLE, below).
  • Even cuts the range into equal slices: turn the jog for the count (2–128), the pads lighting for each as you turn.
  • Transient cuts at the sample's hits: turn the jog for Sens — lower keeps only the strongest, higher every small one — and watch the slices move on the wave; the count shows top right (128+ past the first 128).
  • Lazy chops by ear. Pad 1 lights white; tap it and the range plays. The next pad is always the white one: tap it to drop a slice where the sample is. The slices so far stay lit. It ends at the range's end, on Back or on a click. Back before the first tap changes nothing.
  • Clear all — asks Clear all slices?; Yes leaves one slice, the range, as a fresh load.
  • Convert to kit (below).

In Even and Transient, Back keeps the cut; a click keeps it and goes straight into the slice editor at the same view, to nudge, add or remove a slice.

On page 3, a click (or Shift + click) opens the SAMPLE menu: Load sample, Trim — cuts the file to the range and keeps your slices, each on the same sound (a slice wholly outside the range has no audio left and goes, its steps joining the nearest slice kept) — and Normalize. Trim and Normalize ask New or Overwrite, as on an Audio clip.

A slice's sound settings belong to its number. Adding or removing a slice renumbers the steps of every clip of the track, so each keeps playing the same piece of the sample. One Undo takes back a whole visit to a chopping tool or the slice editor — every slice it made or moved, and every clip's steps with them.

Delete + click resets the page showing: page 1 the picked slice's Play, Pitch, Detune, Revrs and Gain (with Shift, every slice's Play and Revrs), page 2 its Attk and Decay (with Shift, every slice's), page 3 the sample's Gain, Pitch and Detune. A reset takes the automation lanes of what it reset with it, and one Undo brings it all back.

Automation: the sample's Gain, Pitch, Detune and Tempo automate as an Audio clip's do, and every slice's Attack, Decay, Revrs and Play (Shift held) — while such a lane plays, every slice plays at the lane's value, and on Stop each goes back to its own. A single slice's own sound isn't automated. A Slicer's sample is every clip's, so a lane only ever holds it while it plays — it never rewrites the setting.

Convert to kit makes a Move drum rack preset from the slices: a pad for each slice inside the range, up to 32, in order. First the sample is resampled as it sounds — just the range, stretched to the project's tempo if Sync is Warp, retuned by Sync Pitch and the sample's Pitch and Detune, at its Gain — into Samples → dAVEBOx → Exported kits (it takes a moment; the screen says Baking). Every pad plays its slice of that file; the preset goes to Track Presets → dBx-slice, named after the project and track. Move's own drum tracks load it and play the first 16 pads (all 32 stay in the preset); an instrument that loads Move drum racks with more pads, such as DR32, gets them all. Each pad takes its slice's own Pitch, Detune, Gain, Attk and Decay, and Play (One plays the pad through, Thru on to the range's end; Gate holds it as long as you do). A slice set to Revrs plays from a second file, the resample reversed (… rev), so a kit holds at most two. A slice crossing Start or End keeps only the part inside, as it plays. The pads cut each other off, as the slices do. Unlike a slice, a pad responds to velocity, as a stock kit's does: a full-velocity hit is the slice's level, softer hits quieter. Turning a pad's velocity amount up past that can clip on hard hits, as it can on any Move kit.

The SLICER editor works as an instrument's editor: Back returns to the bank you were on, and the sequence keeps working while it is up — tap or hold steps, Record, and hold a step + jog right for its step page. The Shift shortcuts work here as anywhere: Shift + a step or Shift + jog leaves it and does what it always does.

#SAMPLE

SAMPLE is an Audio clip's editor — the track's instrument. Open it from the bank map's SAMPLE pad (where INST is on other tracks) or its instrument pad, by clicking the instrument row in the track's sound menu, or with the instrument shortcut (Shift + hold Note/Session). It follows the clip. (A Slicer's editor is the SLICER editor, above.)

  • No sample: Click to load sample — a click opens the sample chooser.
  • Audio: the clip's waveform. K1 Start · K2 Zoom · K3 End — both a screen pixel a detent, a single sample when zoomed all the way in. Start and End mark the loop, for a sample that isn't a perfect loop: nothing past End sounds. End reads Off until you turn it down; it goes as far as the end of the sample, and one detent past that turns it Off again. Moving End never changes the speed — Bars (on TIME) does that. Start and End are lines on the waveform; the audio outside them stays on screen, dotted, so you can see what you're cutting (zoom in to scroll before Start). The clip's Length is set with the Loop gestures (see Clip length & the loop), by the bar or the step, and works as a sequence's loop does: it picks which part of the loop plays and for how long. A clip longer than the loop plays it once and is silent until it comes round — a 1-bar loop in a 2-bar clip plays one bar, then rests one. K5 Pitch · K6 Detune · K8 Gain set the whole sample, and K7 its Tempo, 1 BPM a detent (Shift: 0.1) — what Warp follows. K4 is Offset (as on the TIME page): where in the audio the clip starts, marked by a small arrow on top of the waveform — stopped, the playhead rests there, and step 1 plays from it. The waveform itself never moves. The knob in hand reads out at the top, and the waveform is drawn at the gain it plays at. Zoomed in, the view stays on what you touched last.

Zoomed all the way out, an Audio clip's SAMPLE screen is the clip: from Start for its Length, the audio drawn where it lands at the sample's Tempo — squeezed or stretched as you turn Tempo, empty where the Length runs past the end of the sample — with a tick under it for each beat and a taller one for each bar. A margin either side shows a little of the sample before Start and after the clip, dithered, so you can see where you are in the file.

SAMPLE has three pages: turn the jog for the next (the header reads 1/3, 2/3, 3/3). The waveform is page 1; pages 2 and 3 show every name and value at once, two rows of four, each setting on the same knob as on page 1 where page 1 has it:

K1K2K3K4
TIME, top rowSyncWarpNudgeOffset
TIME, bottom rowTempoBars
SOUND, bottom rowPitchDetuneGain

(SOUND's top row is empty.)

  • Sync — Grid (the default): the clip keeps to the sequencer, fitted to the tempo; or Free (below). It works with Loop and Shot alike.
  • Warp — how the speed is changed: Vintage, Pitch or Warp (above); on a Free clip Pitch (speed and pitch together, as a tape) or Warp (the time alone).
  • Nudge — moves the sample against the bar, 5 ms a detent (Shift: 1).
  • Offset — where in the audio the clip starts, a step (of the clip's resolution) a detent, read as a note value: 3/16 is three 1/16 steps in. Step 1 plays from there, and what lies before it comes round at the end of the loop. The waveform stays as it is; stopped, the playhead rests at the Offset point, and the beat ticks count from it. The pads, which follow the clip, start from it too.

Touch Offset, Tempo or Bars and the clip's waveform comes up over the page while you hold it — Start and End, the Offset arrow, the beats — so you see what the turn does. A knob that does nothing on this clip reads --: on a Free clip, Bars.

Tempo and Bars sit in a frame together: both describe the sample itself, not the clip. Bars is how many bars Start to End (or to the end of the sample, with End Off) lasts — whole bars a detent, odd numbers too. Set it and the Tempo follows, so the loop plays in time; move Start or End afterwards and Bars stays put, the Tempo adjusting. Until you set it, Bars reads what the Tempo makes of the sample (1.7), and the first detent lands on the whole bar that way. Turning Tempo hands the speed back to it, and Bars reads what the new Tempo makes. A small arrow after Tempo or Bars marks the one in charge — the one that stays put when Start or End moves.

For a sample that isn't neatly cut: set Start on the first beat, End where the loop repeats, then Bars to how long that is. The clip's length is separate — make it as long as you want the clip to run.

Gain, Pitch, Detune, Tempo and the CLIP bank's Dir can be automated like any knob (see Automation): record them, or hold a step and turn. While a lane plays, the knob shows the value it is playing at and the sound follows it; the setting comes back on Stop. A lane on Dir turns the loop round at its step.

A Free clip (TIME page Sync: Free) plays off the sequencer's timing. Launched with the clip, it plays Start to End on its own at the sample's own speed: the project's tempo, the clip's length and its loop round don't touch it, so a loop of any length drifts against the beat as it likes. With Mode Loop it loops Start to End for as long as the clip plays; with Mode Shot it plays Start to End once, then the clip stops — even when that is longer than the clip. TIME then reads:

  • Warp — Pitch changes speed and pitch together, as a tape does (faster is higher); Warp changes the time alone, at the same pitch.
  • Speed (on Tempo's knob) — 1–400 % of the sample's own, 1 % a detent (Shift: 0.1 %). K7 on page 1 turns it too. Touching it shows no waveform: it changes how fast the sample plays, not what the waveform shows.
  • Offset and Nudge work as on the grid: a launch starts that far into Start..End (the Offset measured at the sample's Tempo, wrapping round inside Start..End), less the Nudge. The Offset arrow is on the waveform.

Pitch and Detune still tune it, so on Warp, time and pitch are fully apart. Bars reads -- (there's no grid), and the waveform shows Start to End with no beats. The Tempo, Bars and Warp you had are kept, so switching back to Grid puts them where they were. REMIX works on bars, so it has nothing to do on a Free clip: its settings are kept and read --. A Warp start is about 15 ms after the launch (the stretcher needs a head start); a Pitch start is on the launch.

Touch Tempo and click (page 1 or TIME) for Tempo's menu (not on a Free clip, whose knob there is Speed):

  • Fit to clip (an Audio clip's) — sets Bars to the clip's length, so Start to End (or the end of the sample) lasts exactly as long as the clip, and Warp stretches it to fit. It fits once: change the clip's length afterwards and Bars stay as they are. One Undo puts it back. A fit outside 0.1–999.9 BPM says Out of range.
  • Original tempo — the sample's Tempo becomes the project's, so it plays exactly as recorded.

A click on SAMPLE's waveform page opens its menu (Shift + click does the same):

  • Load sample — the chooser (below).
  • Trim — cuts the file to what the clip plays, Start for its Length (Start moves to the beginning).
  • Normalize — raises the file's loudest point to full scale.

Trim and Normalize ask New (the default: a new sample, named … trim or … norm, the original kept in the project) or Overwrite (the project's copy itself — everything using it changes). Back changes nothing. Both write a 16-bit WAV; the settings stay. If one can't be done the sample stays and the screen says why (NOT NORMALIZED / Nothing to raise on a silent file). Back leaves SAMPLE. The Shift shortcuts work here as anywhere: Shift + a step or Shift + jog leaves SAMPLE and does what it always does.

Choosing a sample: the list starts with This project (samples it already holds), dAVEBOx Resample, Recordings, Samples and the Core Library; turn and click into a folder. The file under the cursor plays as you rest on it (WAV or AIFF). Click a file to pick it: dAVEBOx copies it into the project, so the project keeps its sounds when copied or when the library changes. None clears the clip — on a Slicer it asks first (the sample and its slices go; the steps stay). An Audio clip takes samples up to 30 minutes; a Slicer up to 4. A sample longer than a minute plays from the card as it goes, so a long one costs little memory. Starting the transport partway through an Audio clip, changing Dir or moving Start or Length while it plays can leave a few milliseconds of silence before it comes in, on time. A sample whose file has gone reads Missing: name and stays silent.

#The banks

BankKnobs
CLIP, SlicerAs a melodic clip's (Res, Strch, Shift, InQnt, Crop›, Dir), with >Seq› on K8 (touch, click): one step per slice, each at its place at the sample's Tempo, so the clip plays the sample back as it was — now as slices you can rearrange. A clip whose length you never set grows to hold all of it (a coarser resolution past 256 steps); a length you set stays, and the slices past it wait beyond the loop's end. No Legato: a step holds one slice
CLIP, AudioMode · Strch · K7 Dir; everything else about the sample is on SAMPLE's pages. Dir is a MIDI clip's: Fwd, Bwd (the sample backwards), PPf and PPb (ping-pong: a pass forwards, the next backwards, in turn — PPb starts backwards). A Shot plays one pass, so it offers Fwd and Bwd alone; a ping-pong set before plays as its first way, and comes back when you switch to Loop. Mode is Loop (the clip plays round and round) or Shot: a one-shot — launched, the clip plays its length once from its top, then stops, so it can be fired off like a sample; launch it again to replay it. Every other setting stays as it is when you switch. Strch works as a sequence's does, in audio: x2 doubles the clip's Length and the sample's Tempo — the loop plays at half speed across twice the bars; /2 the reverse. With Bars set, Bars double instead of the Tempo, with the same result. On a Free clip Strch x2 halves the Speed (/2 doubles it). Past 256 steps or the Tempo's range it says BEAT STRETCH / EXPAND LIMIT (or COMPRESS LIMIT). Touch Strch and the clip's waveform comes up over the bank while you hold it (not on a Free clip). Delete + click puts Mode back to Loop and Dir to Fwd
PAD MODE (Slicer)Layout: 4 Rows or 16 Pads, how the slices sit on the pads
LIVE ARPAs on a melodic track, but Step replaces Oct: each repeat moves one slice up (or down), up to 15
REMIX (both)Rearranges the loop as it plays — see REMIX below
NOTE FX (Slicer)As on a drum track — nothing that changes a pitch. Quant lives here only

There's no RPT GROOVE, HARMONY, SEQ ARP, DELAY or MIDI FX on either kind. The step editor's first knob reads Slice n and picks the step's slice; on a Slicer, K2–K4 are the step's Pitch, Length / Start and Dir (above).

#REMIX

REMIX chops the bar up and plays it back rearranged — reversed bits, stutters, breaks and pitch jumps — without changing your clip. It's in the bank map's FX column, third pad, on Audio and Slicer tracks alike, and each clip has its own.

KnobDoes
K1 RemixOff / On (turn deliberately)
K2 ChopHow the bar is cut into pieces, from big to small: 10+6 (two pieces, 10 and 6 sixteenths long), 6+6+4, … 8ths, … 16ths
K3 OrderWhere the pieces go — numbered from the gentlest (a phrase repeated) to the wildest (pieces from all over); Rev plays the whole bar backwards. How many there are depends on the Chop. Touch K3 + click opens Presets…: the 80 remixes of the Yamaha RS7000 (Normal, Reverse, Roll, Break, Pitch, 1–16 each) — the jog picks, a click loads one (its Order and all its amounts), Back leaves things as they were
K4 ShuflHow many pieces follow the Order: 0 % plays the bar as written, 100 % the whole Order
K5 RevrsHow much of what plays runs backwards
K6 StutrHow many stutters (quick repeats) play. Touch K6 + click turns it to Rate — Orig, 1/32, 1/64, how fast they repeat — then to Vel: On, the repeats ramp in level as the RS7000's do; Off, every repeat at full level
K7 GapsHow many gaps cut into the bar. Touch K7 + click turns it to Depth: how hard a gap cuts, from 100 % (silent) down to a slight shortening
K8 PitchHow far the pitched pieces move, −24 to +24 semitones: below 0 they go the other way — what went up goes down

Delete + click puts the clip's REMIX back as a new clip has it: Off, the first Chop and Order, its amounts. One Undo brings it back.

Every amount works on what you hear: each turn up changes something that plays, on any Order, and the same settings always give the same bar. The effects combine — reverse a few pieces of an Order, then add a stutter. A change lands at the next bar line. Turning any REMIX knob shows a pop-up over the page: the knob's name and value across the top, then the bar it makes — a column per 1/16, as tall as the part of the loop it plays (in order, they rise like a stair), hollow when reversed, dotted when stuttered, narrow when cut short, empty when silent, with a caret when pitched and a tick under each piece's start. The line under it names the Chop and how much of the bar the Order moves (6/16 MOVED), or OFF while REMIX is off. It goes when you let go. On an Audio clip the pads follow: the 1/16 you're hearing pulses, the rest dim.

On a Slicer, REMIX rearranges your steps bar by bar — a remixed step plays its slice reversed or pitched as the remix says, on top of its own sound. To keep a remix, bake it (§16.1): on an Audio clip that records it into a new sample, on a Slicer it writes the remixed steps, reversals and pitches into the clip. Either way REMIX turns off, so it isn't applied twice.

#Copying, clearing and undo

Copying follows the kind:

  • An Audio clip onto an Audio clip carries its sample and settings.
  • An Audio clip onto a Slicer that has no sample gives the Slicer that sample: the part the clip plays becomes the Slicer's range, cut into 16 even slices and laid on the clip's steps in order, so it sounds just as the loop did — then move them around. Pitch, Detune, Gain and Tempo come too; Sync Pitch stays Pitch, Warp stays Warp (on a sample up to a minute), Vintage becomes Off. A Slicer that has a sample refuses it (CAN'T PASTE): clear it with None first.
  • A Slicer's clip onto another Slicer's carries its steps (and its automation) — they play the destination's slices.
  • A Slicer's clip onto an Audio clip gives that clip the Slicer's sample; the steps don't come (an Audio clip has none).
  • Nothing crosses between these and a MIDI or drum track, and a cut stays on its own kind.

Delete + clip on an Audio clip asks Remove sample? first (No is selected); Yes clears the sample, and Undo brings it back. On a Slicer it clears the steps; the sample is the track's and stays. Shift + Delete + clip resets it completely — on an Audio track, sample and all; on a Slicer the sample is the track's and stays. Undo covers the sample too: loading one, None, Shift + Delete, Resample In place, Flatten track (one Undo for every clip), a Trim or Normalize to a New sample, a visit to a chopping tool or the slice editor, and pasting an Audio clip onto a Slicer each come back with one Undo. Turning a setting isn't an undo step of its own, and an Overwrite can't be undone. Choosing another instrument clears the track's steps and lets go of its samples, asking first — and one Undo brings it all back. Export to Ableton brings both kinds across as Live audio tracks — see §16.3.

Track View at rest shows an Audio clip as SAMPLE does zoomed out — its bars across, the audio where it lands at the sample's Tempo, the beats under it and the playhead moving through — and its Tempo on the line above (Loop 112; a Free clip shows its Speed instead: Loop Free 100%, Shot Free 50%); a Slicer shows the page bar and playhead, as any sequenced track does.

Purge samples. Samples you no longer use stay in the project. Project Settings → Purge samples removes every one that no clip, no Slicer, no undo step and no saved state uses, after saying how many and how much space it frees.

#Recording into an Audio clip

On an Audio track, Rec records the Move's audio input (the line-in jack, or the built-in mic when nothing is plugged in) into the active clip.

  • An empty clip records until you press Rec again, and stops at the end of that bar (up to 64 bars). The clip becomes that many bars long.
  • A clip that has a sample records a new layer: one pass of the clip, with what you play mixed over the clip as you hear it. Pitch, Start, Dir, Speed, REMIX and the rest are baked into the new sample, which the clip then plays as it is (Mode and Free stay as they were: the file is the pass you heard). On a Shot clip the take is its one pass, and on a Free one-shot however long that pass runs. Press Rec during the pass to stop adding to it: what you played stays, the rest of the pass keeps the old sound.
  • Stopped, Rec gives MIDI's one-bar count-in, then records from the top. Playing, the take waits for the clip's next loop (the next bar on an empty clip), and the heading shows WAIT; while it records it shows REC and the bar. Rec blinks red while it waits and is solid red while it records. The clip's pad in Session View blinks white while it waits and pulses white while it records. In Track View the pads go white: recording into an empty clip, one pad a bar (the bars recorded bright, the one recording pulsing, the rest of a set Length dim); a clip with a sample keeps its sections, the part recorded so far bright, the playhead pulsing, the rest dim.
  • You hear the input through the track's effects and fader while the take runs. The take itself is recorded without them.
  • The take is saved as a new sample in the project, so Undo brings back the clip as it was. Stopping the transport cancels a take; a take that heard nothing is dropped.
  • The INPUT bank (the green pad above SAMPLE on the pad map) sets the input. Monitor, Input and Gain are one setting for the whole Move — the same three are in Project Settings, so you can set them with no Audio track at all; Length and Overdub are the track's, saved with the project: | Knob | Does | Choices | |---|---|---| | K1 Monitor | When you hear the input | Off · Rec (through the track while a take runs) · On (always: straight to the output, through the track while a take runs) | | K2 Input | Both channels, or one on both sides | Stereo · Mono L · Mono R | | K3 Gain | The input's level, for the take and what you hear | −24 to +24 dB (0) | | K4 Length | How long a take into an empty clip is | Free (until Rec again) · 1 · 2 · 4 · 8 bars | | K5 Overdub | A take into a clip that has a sample | Layer (over what it plays) · Replace | Delete + click puts all five back to the defaults in bold. While INPUT is up, the track's overview shows the input's level where the waveform is, and CLIP when it reaches full scale. The Move picks the source itself: line-in when a cable is plugged in, else the built-in mic.
  • With Replace, the clip's sound is left out while you record and comes back after a punch-out (Rec during the pass).
  • With the speakers on and nothing plugged into line-in, the Move asks first: the mic would hear the speakers. On a Slicer, Rec still records slices from the pads.
