Chapter 8

Clip Timing & Grid

These banks set a clip's grid, timing and playback — CLIP on a melodic track, DRUM LANE and ALL LANES on a drum track. Parameters marked Rewrites notes change your notes permanently (Undo reverses them); the rest only change how the clip plays.

Resetting a bank is covered in Parameter banks.

#8.1 CLIP bank

Video

Tutorial 3.3: The CLIP bank (from 2:36)

A melodic clip's grid, direction, and note transforms.

KnobOn screenWhat it doesRewrites notesDefault
1RESResolution — keeps the pattern's steps and changes how long a step is. Alt (ZOOM): keeps the timing and changes how many steps it takes (needs the loop at step 1).Yes1/16
2STRCHStretch — turn right to double the clip, left to halve it; one change per touch (let go to do it again). Refused (COMPRESS LIMIT) when notes would collide, and doubling is refused past step 256. Needs the loop at step 1 (LOOP STARTS AFTER STEP 1 / CROP FIRST). Doubling is also refused (NOTES PAST THE LOOP END / CROP FIRST) if notes lie past the loop's end.Yes—
3SHIFTShift — rotate the notes in the loop by whole steps; a note pushed off the loop's end comes round to its start. Alt (NUDGE): finer. Needs the loop at step 1.Yes0
4LGTOLegato — touch the knob and click the jog; lengthens every note in the loop to reach the next (the last to the loop's end). Turning it does nothing. Needs the loop at step 1.Yes—
5INQNTInput Quantize — snap recorded notes to the grid (Off, 1/64 … 1/4t). One value per track, shared with ALL LANES.NoOff
6CROPCrop — touch the knob and click the jog: the loop becomes the whole clip — it moves to step 1 and everything outside it is removed (automation too). One Undo. Turning it does nothing.Yes—
7DIRDirection — Forward, Backward, or ping-pong. Alt (REVRS): Reverse Style.NoFwd
8IMPRTImport MIDI — touch the knob and click the jog to fill a clip from a MIDI file — see Import a MIDI file. Turning it does nothing.Yes—

Direction is Forward, Backward, or one of two ping-pong modes (they differ only in which end they start from). Reverse Style (the alt of Dir) sets what backward playback does to each note:

  • Step (default) reverses the order of the steps; each note still triggers at its start and sounds unchanged.
  • Audio also mirrors each note within its slot — note-on at the note's end, note-off at its start — for a tape-reverse feel. In ping-pong, Audio plays the endpoints twice, so every note gets one forward and one reversed pass.

Recording needs Forward direction; bake and export freeze the direction into the notes and reset it to Forward.

#8.2 DRUM LANE bank

Video

Tutorial 2.2: Euclidean rhythms and per-lane loops (from 1:39)

The selected lane's grid — the drum counterpart to the CLIP bank.

KnobOn screenWhat it doesRewrites notesDefault
1RESResolution. Alt: ZOOM.Yes1/16
2STRCHStretch. Doubling is refused (NOTES PAST THE LOOP END / CROP FIRST) if hits lie past the loop's end.Yes—
3SHIFTShift. Alt: NUDGE.Yes0
4LGTOLegato (this lane) — touch the knob and click the jog.Yes—
5EUCLDEuclid — spread N hits evenly across the lane. Hand-placed hits on steps the pattern does not use stay; a hand-placed hit on a step it lands on becomes part of it, and turning Euclid down removes it. Try it on an empty lane, and pair it with Shift (knob 3) for variations.Yes0
6CROPCrop (this lane) — touch the knob and click the jog.Yes—

Lane length is Loop + jog; the lane's MIDI note is on the NOTE FX bank. Zoom, Stretch, Shift and Legato need the lane's loop at step 1 — Crop puts it there.

#8.3 ALL LANES bank

Applies one setting to all 32 lanes at once. It opens like any other bank: the knobs, Loop and the Shift + Step shortcuts act on every lane straight away. Touch Shift or Dir and click the jog to switch that knob to its Alt.

KnobOn screenWhat it doesRewrites notes
1RESResolution for all lanesYes
2STRCHStretch all lanes (NO ROOM if any can't fit; doubling is refused if hits lie past the loop's end — crop first)Yes
3SHIFTShift. Alt: NUDGE.Yes
4QUANTQuantize all lanes at playbackNo
5CROPCrop every lane — touch the knob and click the jogYes
6INQNTRecording input quantize for the trackNo
7DIRDirection for all lanes. Alt (REVRS): Reverse Style.No
8RSYNCRepeat Sync — held repeats wait for the beat grid (On) or fire at once (Off)No

Stretch and Shift are refused (LOOP STARTS AFTER STEP 1 / CROP FIRST) if any lane's loop starts later than step 1. The track's velocity input (VelIn) is on TRACK CONFIG and Shift + Step 10.

Chapter 9

Sequencer Effects

Video

Tutorial 4.5: The signal flow (from 6:25)

The sequencer effects work on notes, before they reach the instrument — for audio effects such as reverb, see FX 1–4. Two kinds shape notes beyond the stored clip:

  • Sequencer effects (§9.1–9.4) reshape every note — sequenced or live — at playback, per clip. They're non-destructive: return a knob to its default and the clip plays exactly as written.
  • Live input modifiers (§9.5) act only on what you play live, before it's sequenced: LIVE ARP on melodic tracks, and on drums Note Repeat, shaped by RPT GROOVE.

Drum tracks have NOTE FX and DELAY only. A knob marked Alt switches to its alternate when you touch it and click the jog; Back switches it back.

Everything runs one chain — the live modifier first, then the effects:

 LIVE INPUT ──▶ [LIVE ARP / Note Repeat] ──┐
                                           ├─▶ NOTE FX ─▶ HARMONY ─▶ DELAY ─▶ SEQ ARP ─▶ OUT
 SEQUENCED NOTES ──────────────────────────┘

A track's MIDI FX module comes before all of this. Set to Post (the default), it plays first and the effects work on what it plays; set to Pre, it sits on what you play live, before LIVE ARP and before recording — see Position — Pre or Post in Editing a module.

The global groove is applied after the chain; Performance Mode comes last.

#9.1 NOTE FX

Video

Tutorial 4.1: NOTE FX and HARMONY

Melodic & drum.

Shifts every note's pitch, velocity, timing, and length.

KnobOn screenWhat it doesDefault
1OCTOctave shift (±4)0
2OFFSTNote offset — scale degrees or semitones (±24)0
3VELVelocity offset (±127)0
4QUANTQuantize at playback (0–100 %)0 %
5LEN>Fixed note length in step-multiples (-- = as written)--
6GATEScale the length, 0–400 % — under 100 % shortens, over 100 % lengthens100 %
7—(empty)
8RANDPitch randomness (0–24; -- at 0). Alt (ALGO): Pure (even spread), Gaus (clusters near the note) or Walk (drifts from note to note)--

On a drum track, knobs 1 and 2 (OCT, NOTE) set the selected lane's MIDI note; knobs 3–6 apply to that lane, and 7–8 are empty.

Note

Three kinds of quantize: INQNT (CLIP, ALL LANES) snaps notes as you record them. QUANT (here, and on ALL LANES) pulls notes toward the grid as they play, leaving the clip as written. Shift + Step 16 sets QUANT to 100 %.

Video

Adds up to four voices to every note (0 = off; negative values add the voice below):

  • Knobs 1–8 set each step's pitch offset (±24 scale degrees); with Shift held they set each step's velocity (Thru passes the incoming velocity).
  • On the pads, the column is the step and the row one of four velocity levels, bottom to top. Press the bottom row again to turn the step off; Delete + pad sets Thru.
  • Loop + pad sets the step-loop length (1–8).
  • Turn the jog to close the editor.

#9.5 Live input modifiers

These shape what you play live — on the pads or over external MIDI — before it's sequenced, leaving the stored clip untouched.

#LIVE ARP

Video

Tutorial 4.4: LIVE ARP (from 5:09)

Melodic. Per track.

An arpeggiator for live pad and external input; sequenced notes are left alone. The controls match SEQ ARP (except Retrigger defaults to Off), plus Latch (LATCH, knob 8), which keeps the arp running after you let go:

  • With pads held, tap Loop to latch; tap it again (pads held) to unlatch.
  • Loop with no pads held clears the latched notes but keeps Latch on.
  • Stop, Delete + Play, or switching to Session View unlatches.
  • Shift + Step 11 (tap) toggles LIVE ARP on and off with the last style.
  • Shift + hold Step 11 (about half a second) opens LIVE ARP's page and holds it on screen — the knobs edit it, touch knob 5 + click opens Arp Steps — until Back closes it. LIVE ARP is an ordinary bank: the knobs stay on it after the page closes, and it is on the bank map (IN column, second pad).
  • LIVE ARP can't be automated — its settings belong to the track, not a clip. It is still available as a macro destination.

#RPT GROOVE

Drum. Per lane.

Repeat Groove shapes the 8-step gate mask of a lane's Note Repeat; you hear it while a repeat mode is active.

Touch any knob and click the jog to switch pages; the bottom of the screen says KNB+CLK NUDGE or KNB+CLK VELOCITY, whichever is next.

KnobsScreen pageAfter knob touch + jog click
1–8Velocity per gate step — Thru (the pad's own velocity) or a value 1–127Nudge per gate step (±50 % of the step)

Delete + jog click resets the selected lane's groove, whether or not a repeat mode is on.

Chapter 10

Automation

Video

Tutorial 6.2: Automation (from 1:22) · Tutorial 6.3: Automating sounds and effects (from 4:08)

Almost anything you can turn in dAVEBOx, you can automate — a Schwung instrument's or effect's parameter, a level, a bank knob, or a MIDI target. There's no lane to arm: the knob that plays a parameter records it.

Not a Move instrument's own parameters. On a track that plays one of Move's instruments (Drift, Wavetable, a drum rack…), its sound is edited in Move's own editor, and dAVEBOx can't reach those knobs: holding a step and turning one writes no lock, and recording doesn't capture it. The track's levels, its MACROS (Aftertouch, Pitch Bend) and dAVEBOx's own bank knobs still automate there.

#10.1 Making it

Two ways:

  • Record it. With the transport playing and Record armed, turn a knob: the move is written at the playhead for as long as your hand is on the knob, round the loop as many times as you hold it. Parameters you don't touch keep what they had. Each time you start, a notice says how long the lane you're recording onto is — ● LANE: 2 BAR, or ● LANE: 13 ST when it isn't whole bars — the cycle the move will repeat on. See Recording.
  • Lock a step (a punch). Hold a step and turn a knob: that step takes a lock — the value held flat for the whole step. The parameter jumps to it as the step starts and jumps back to what the lane was doing when it ends. Press a later step while you hold to stretch it across several (see The AUTOMATION screen). See also Editing notes.
  • Place a point. Tap Shift while you hold the step — before or after turning — and a notice says POINT: the step gets a single point instead, which the lane glides into and on from. Tap again for PUNCH. Every hold starts as a punch; the footer says what a tap switches to (SHFT POINT). Holding Shift while you turn is still fine adjustment.
  • See a step's values. While you hold a step, every automated parameter on screen shows the value it plays at that step (a lock, a recorded point, or the glide between them), and goes back to its own value when you let go.
  • Delete + step removes the automation on that step, on every lane. Deleting a punch gives the lane back as it was before it.

Each lane is one envelope. Its points glide into each other, and a lock is where it jumps. Parameters that are a choice or a switch step from value to value instead. A lane starts where its parameter rests: its first point also puts one on the lane's first step, carrying the resting value. At the end of the loop the lane does what its Wrap says (below).

What can be automated: a Schwung module's editor pages, the levels on MIX and in the session mixer, the eight MACROS, and these dAVEBOx bank knobs — CLIP and ALL LANES direction, NOTE FX (all but LEN>), HARMONY, DELAY, and SEQ ARP (all but STEPS) — and an Audio clip's Gain, Pitch, Detune and Tempo on SAMPLE and Dir on its CLIP bank (listed as Smp>Gain and so on), and a Slicer's every-slice settings (Shift on the SLICER editor, listed as Slcs>Attack …); holding one of their steps opens that editor. On a drum track, NOTE FX is set per lane and isn't automated. See Parameter banks and Sequencer Effects.

  • An automated knob shows a dot on its cell and a blinking ring.
  • Mute + touch mutes that parameter's automation; Delete + touch clears it. (In the session mixer, Mute + touch still mutes the track.)
  • The resting value is where a parameter sits when nothing automates it: on Stop, and in clips without automation for it. There's one per parameter on its track. Turn the knob while stopped, or while a clip with no automation for it is playing, and that's the new resting value. While the playing clip does automate it, turning the knob without Record takes the parameter over until you let go.
  • Switching clips returns the old clip's automated parameters to rest; a clip that automates the same parameter starts where its own lane starts, straight away. A parameter whose automation you muted stays where you put it.
  • Projects made before this version are converted when they open and play the same. Once saved, dAVEBOx 1.0.0 opens them without their automation.

#10.2 The AUTOMATION screen

Tap AUTO on the bank map and let go: the screen opens on a list of everything automated in the current clip — parameters, levels, MIDI targets and the pads' aftertouch — with the cursor on the first row. Its knobs do nothing; the jog does everything.

  • Each row shows its cycle, the length it repeats over: 4 BAR, 13 ST (steps, when it isn't whole bars; 13 ST/32 when its steps aren't sixteenths), or CLIP when it follows the clip. A muted row reads OFF, a cleared one EMPTY and its length, and the pads' aftertouch PADS.
  • With nothing automated the list has only + Add lane.

With the cursor on a row, the step buttons, pages and screen show that row's lane, not the clip's notes (click the row for its operations, below):

  • Step buttons are coloured by the value the lane plays on each step — dim for low, bright for high. A step with a point on it blinks off briefly — a lock, the step after a lock (where the lane jumps back), a recorded point, or the lane's first step; steps past the end of the cycle are dark grey.
  • Left / Right page through the lane's own length: a 4-bar lane under a 1-bar clip has four pages. The header shows the cycle and page (2 BAR PG 1/2).
  • The playhead shows where that lane is in its own cycle.
  • Hold any step of the lane to jump to where that parameter is edited — its bank, its module's page (on a per-pad parameter, that pad), MIX for a level, MACROS for a MIDI target or a SnapMorph knob. Turn its knob to set the value on that step, whether it held one or not; let go to come back, on the same row and page. On a bank the header shows <AUTO S7 (step 7). The parameter's cell is highlighted, and while the step is held it shows the value the lane plays there — shown only, the parameter doesn't move until you turn the knob. A module's page keeps its graphics (filter curve, envelope) while you're there. On a bank, MIX, MACROS or a module's page the lane's current page (its 16 steps) is drawn over the half of the screen the parameter isn't in, with the held step marked between dotted lines and the playhead when it's on that page. Its bottom edge is the lane's page bar: one segment a page, the one shown thicker. In a module's editor only the held lane's knob turns while you hold — turning another shows its name with ONLY in the header for a moment — and the editor stays on its page. The footer says what a Shift tap switches to (SHFT POINT / SHFT PUNCH).
  • Hold a step, then press a later one to stretch the held step's value up to and including that step, the way a held note stretches to a tapped step. The value is the one you turned, or — before any turn — what the lane plays on the held step, even between two points. Anything already set in between is replaced. As a punch the range jumps back after its last step to what the lane played there; as a point (Shift tapped) it holds flat to its last step and glides on from there. Left / Right still page the lane while you hold, so the range can reach into later bars. Pressing an earlier step wraps round the end of the cycle. Press the end step again to shorten the range by one, or a step inside it to shorten it there; the steps you give back play what they did before. Turn the knob again while you still hold and the whole range takes the new value. While you hold, every step of the range blinks like a set value. One Undo takes back the whole hold.
  • With Seq Follow on (Play + Left/Right), the lane's page follows its playhead while the transport runs, as the note steps do — except while you're holding a step, which keeps its page. Paging by hand pauses it until you stop.
  • Shift + click a row to jump to where that parameter is edited; Back returns you to this menu, on the same row. The step buttons keep showing the lane there, so you can hold a step and turn the knob to set it, and the bank map still marks AUTO. On a bank, MIX, MACROS or a module's page the lane's current page is drawn there too, as for a held step. In a module's editor only the lane's knob turns (another shows ONLY in the header) and the editor stays on its page until you go Back. Leave that place any other way and the jump is over.
  • Back at the list closes the screen: you return to the bank you were on, and the step buttons show the clip again. Leaving by the bank map (another bank, or an editor from its right-hand pads) does the same — the steps show notes again.

Click a row for its operations. They open as a short menu at the top of the screen, and the rest of the screen shows the lane itself: its whole length as a graph — what it plays, as it plays it — with the page bar along its bottom edge and the playhead running through both. The graph follows each change you make here (Wrap, Loop, Rate, Scale) and new recording.

  • Mute / Unmute.
  • Wrap — what the lane does at the end of its loop. Reset (default) holds the last value to the end, then jumps back to the lane's start. Carry glides from the last point into the start across the loop point. Lanes saved before this change keep the Wrap they had.
  • Link — On (default): the automation is transformed with the note sequence — Resolution and Beat Stretch scale it, Clock Shift and Nudge move it (inside the clip's loop, as they move its notes), doubling the loop copies it forward (so the doubled clip plays as the old loop did twice), and Crop moves it to step 1 with the loop and removes what lay outside (on a drum track, the ALL LANES versions; a lane with its own Loop is left as it is). Off: it stays put whatever you do to the notes.
  • Loop — the parameter's own loop length in steps, or CLIP to follow the clip. It can be shorter than the clip (it repeats inside it) or longer, up to 256 steps (it runs across several passes of the clip). A lane with its own Loop runs in step with the song, and restarts when its clip is launched at Launch 1-bar — see Launching clips.
  • Rate — /16 to ×16, the loop stretching to match.
  • Scale — 0–200 %: how far the lane moves (toward zero, or on a centred parameter like pan or pitch bend, toward and away from its centre).
  • Clear — every value goes, but the lane stays with its settings, its length included (it reads EMPTY and its length, e.g. EMPTY 4 BAR, ready for new values). On a drum track, set Loop on the empty lane and new recording or step input lands at that length.
  • Delete — the lane goes altogether.

The pads' aftertouch row (PADS) has only Delete.

+ Add lane (after the lanes) adds an empty lane, so you can set its Wrap, Loop, Rate and Scale before writing anything into it. Click it and choose the parameter as you would for a macro — a module, a bank, Levels or MIDI (on an Audio track or a Slicer also Sample, and on a Slicer All Slices), then the parameter (see The MACROS bank). You come back to the list with the new lane's operations open; Back from the picker returns without adding one. Choosing a parameter that already has a lane in this clip opens that lane.

With the cursor on a lane, Delete + click clears just that lane (its points go; the row stays). The last row is Clear all: click it to clear everything. Every operation is one undo, and Back closes one layer at a time. Conductor tracks don't have this bank.

On a drum track, automation belongs to the whole track, and each automated parameter has its own cycle, taken from the lane that was selected when you first recorded or locked it:

  • Select a 12-step hat lane and record a filter sweep: the sweep repeats every 12 steps while the 16-step kick carries on around it.
  • The cycle stays put: recording more onto it from another lane, editing it, or changing the lanes' lengths afterwards doesn't change it.
  • Two operations do: Loop sets it in the parameter's own steps (it can run longer than any lane — it plays in full), and Match pad makes it the selected lane's.
  • ALL LANES Clock Shift, Nudge, Resolution, Beat Stretch and Double move each parameter's automation inside its own cycle.
  • The clip as a whole runs the length of its longest lane; shorter lanes loop inside it.

Copying or cutting a clip takes its automation with it. To another track, automation of the track's levels and of dAVEBOx's own knobs always comes along; automation of an instrument or effect parameter comes along only when the destination has the same instrument or effect in the same place. Anything left behind is counted in a notice (AUTOMATION / 1 LANE NOT CARRIED).

#10.3 MIDI targets

A macro can point at Aftertouch or Pitch Bend on any track, and at any MIDI CC on a MIDI track. They record, lock, mute and clear like any other parameter and appear in the AUTOMATION list by name — see the MACROS bank. Aftertouch played from the pads is recorded on its own and shows in the list as its own row.

Previous9. Sequencer EffectsNext11. Arranging
Chapter 11

Arranging

Video

Tutorial 1.2: Clips, scenes and the session grid (from 1:09)

Arranging happens in Session View: the clip grid on the pads, 8 tracks across and 4 rows visible. + and − scroll one row at a time through all 16 rows. The eight knobs are a mixer, one per track. What they set — Volume, Pan, Send A or Send B — is the MIXER column of the Session View bank map: hold the jog and tap one.

#11.1 Launching clips

Clips launch at once by default. To have them wait for the next beat or bar, set Launch in Project Settings.

GestureResult
Tap a clipLaunch it (queued until the next boundary, if Launch waits)
Tap the playing clipStop it at the end of its page (tap again to cancel)
Tap a queued clipCancel the launch
Tap an empty clipSwitch the track to it — the track goes quiet, and recording lands there
Shift + clipOpen it in Track View. While stopped, a clip with notes opens without launching; an empty clip launches.
Copy + clip, then anotherCopy the clip (Shift + Copy cuts)
Delete + clipClear its notes (it keeps playing); on an Audio clip, asks to remove its sample
Shift + Delete + clipReset the clip completely
  • Launching a clip replaces whatever was playing on that track.
  • Where a launched clip starts depends on Launch in Project Settings. At 1-bar it starts from its beginning — its notes, every drum lane, and any automation lane with its own Loop. At every other setting (Now, 1/16 … 1/2) it launches in step with the song: it plays from wherever it would be had it been running since you pressed Play.
  • Switching to a track launches its current clip only if that clip is empty.
  • Keep holding Copy to paste one clip into several slots; releasing Copy empties the clipboard.

#11.2 Scenes

A scene launches one clip from every track at once — tap a side button (left of the grid) or a step button (1–16). Shift + side button launches at the end of the current page. Launching a scene switches every track to that row, so a track whose clip there is empty falls silent.

GestureResult
Copy + side button, then a rowCopy all 8 clips
Shift + Copy + side buttonCut the row
Capture + side buttonSnapshot the playing clips into the row
Delete + side buttonClear the row's notes
Shift + Delete + side buttonReset the row's clips

#11.3 Mute & solo

Video

Tutorial 5.1: Mutes and mute snapshots

In Session View each knob stands for its track:

GestureResult
Mute + touch knob 1–8Mute that track
Shift + Mute + touch knobSolo it
Delete + MuteClear every mute and solo
  • A live pad you hold still plays through a muted track.
  • The knob LEDs show each track's state: its color when playing, dark when muted, blinking when soloed.
  • Mute the active track directly in Track View; mute a drum lane in Drum Clips.

#11.4 Mute snapshots

Video

Tutorial 5.1: Mutes and mute snapshots

Store up to 16 mute/solo states; they persist across reboots. In Session View, hold Mute and the step buttons light (grey = empty, yellow = saved):

GestureResult
Mute + Shift + stepSave the current mute/solo state
Mute + stepRecall it
Mute + Delete + stepClear that slot

For snapshots of the sound itself, see Sound snapshots.

#11.5 Volume

  • Volume controls Move's master output, everywhere.
  • Shift + Volume sets the active track's volume, also everywhere — Track View, Session View and the sound editor.
  • A chain track's level and a Move track's mixer level are the same values the mixer rows show, saved with the project.
  • A MIDI track sends standard MIDI volume (CC 7) on its channel out the USB port. A track that plays another track's instrument has no output of its own and says so.
Previous10. AutomationNext12. The Conductor
Chapter 12

The Conductor

Video

Tutorial 5.3: The Conductor (from 2:26)

A Conductor transposes every playing melodic clip in real time, following the note it plays: sequence a progression on it and every responding track follows.

  • It sends no MIDI of its own; its sequence and live pads only steer the transposition.
  • The other tracks' written notes never change — the shift is live.
  • A project can hold one Conductor at a time.

#12.1 Creating one

Shift + click the track's Instmt/Dest row in its TRACK CONFIG menu (the row the menu opens on, just below MIDI FX), and choose Conductor, just after the Move instruments.

  • The transport must be stopped, and it asks first (Make Conductor?).
  • Its notes carry over; its effects, arps and automation reset.
  • If another track is already the Conductor, the screen says which — route that one back first.
  • Mute pauses conducting; the responders snap back to their written pitch.

A Conductor's TRACK CONFIG menu has only the Instmt/Dest row and the track's own settings — no FX slots, mixer controls, LFOs or presets. The track's instrument is parked: choose an instrument from the same picker and it returns with everything attached, and the track is ordinary again.

#12.2 How the shift works

Zero transposition is the project's root note in middle C's octave (C3). On a new Conductor that note sits mid-grid — in a seven-note scale, the second row's fifth pad (and the same note on the third row's second pad and the bottom row's last). The bottom-left pad is an octave down.

  • Play the root and nothing shifts; play higher and the responders rise, lower and they fall.
  • The Conductor's own octave scales the move: an octave up on the Conductor is an octave of transposition.
  • The shift follows the global Scale Aware setting — by scale degree (staying in key) when on, by semitone when off.
  • Between Conductor notes the responders return to zero, unless Cond Lock is on (below). A muted Conductor always holds them at zero.
  • Drum tracks never respond.
  • Audio tracks respond by playing their audio higher or lower — and so does a Slicer with its Cndct switch on (off by default), never by changing which slice plays. The move is in semitones: with Scale Aware on, as far as the key's root moves by the Conductor's degrees. On Next a slice takes the new pitch as it starts and an Audio clip when it comes round; on Now what is sounding moves at once. An Audio clip in Pitch sync keeps its tempo's speed, so it does not move.

#12.3 The Conductor's banks

A Conductor has six banks on its map, starting on CLIP; its CONFIG (the TRACK CONFIG menu) is on the bank map. ON/OFF, OCTAVE, TIMING and Cond Lock belong to the Conductor's current clip, so different Conductor clips can steer different tracks:

BankControls
CLIPThe clip's timing and direction, with Cond Lock (CDLK) on knob 6: Off holds the shift only for each note's length; Lock holds it until the next Conductor note.
STEPEdits the held step, as on any track.
NOTE FXShapes the Conductor's note before the shift is worked out — an octave, an offset, and a per-note random amount. Knobs 3–6 show -.
ON/OFFAn on/off cell per track (TR1…TR8) — on (the default) means the track follows. A drum track's cell is empty; the Conductor's own reads CNDCT.
OCTAVEA per-track octave (−4…+4) added on top of the shift while the Conductor sounds.
TIMINGPer track: Next (a responder takes the shift at its next note) or Now (a sounding note is retriggered at the new pitch at once).

#12.4 Making it permanent

When you bake a scene or export to Live, an Apply Conductor? step can fold the transposition into the responding clips. The Conductor track itself has no bake and exports as a silent placeholder.

Previous11. ArrangingNext13. Performance Mode
Chapter 13

Performance Mode

Video

Tutorial 5.2: Performance Mode (from 1:13)

Performance Mode grabs a short loop of what's playing and lets you transform it live from a grid of effects. It runs in Session View.

#13.1 Entering and exiting

  • Tap Loop to lock it on hands-free; hold Loop to use it only while held.
  • Tap Loop, Back or Note/Session to leave. The captured loop stops, but latched mods stay on for next time.
  • Shift + Loop toggles Latch.
  • The header shows the recalled preset (Slot 12 for one of yours) or Performance; under it are the engaged mods, or NO MODS ENGAGED.

#13.2 The grid

   top row      wild mods        — blue
                velocity / gate  — yellow
                pitch mods       — magenta (melodic only)
   bottom row   length · hold · sync · latch

The bottom row sets the capture length and mode:

PadSets
1–5Capture length: a 1/32, 1/16, 1/8, 1/4 or 1/2 note
6Hold — keep the loop while you hold this pad
7Sync — clock-aligned capture
8Latch — sticky mods

Sync and Latch start on. Shift + a length pad keeps that length looping after you let go; lengths stack, and Hold clears them.

The three mod rows transform the loop. With Latch on, tapping a mod pad toggles it on until you tap it again; with Latch off, a mod runs only while you hold its pad. Press a lit pad to turn its mod off.

Pitch mods (magenta, melodic only)
PadNameEffect
1Oct UpAlternates octave up / original
2Oct DownAlternates octave down / original
3Scale Up+1/+2/+3 scale degrees over 3 loops, then resets
4Scale Down−1/−2/−3 over 3 loops
5FifthUp 4, 8, then 12 scale degrees (stacked fifths), then resets
6TritoneUp 3, 6, then 9 scale degrees over 3 loops, then resets
7Drift±1 random walk, drifts to ±6
8StormRandom ±6 scale degrees per note — chaotic, in key
Velocity / gate mods (yellow, all tracks)
PadNameEffect
1Decrescendo−15 % velocity each loop, down to 10 %
2Swell16-loop triangle
3Crescendo+15 % velocity each loop, up to full
4PulseEven loops full, odd loops 20 %
5Sidechain−15 % per successive note in a loop
6StaccatoGates to 1/8 of the loop
7LegatoGates to the full loop
8Ramp GateGate ramps up across notes
Wild mods (blue)
PadNameEffect
1Half TimeEvery other loop dropped
23 SkipEvery third loop dropped
3PhantomGhost note an octave below, ¼ velocity
4Sparse~50 % of notes dropped
5Glitch±2 scale-degree shift per note
6StaggerNotes offset +0, +1, +2… scale degrees
7ShufflePitch/hit order shuffled each loop
8BackwardsPitch/hit order reversed each loop

#13.3 Which tracks it captures

A track feeds Performance Mode when its Looper setting is on (Track settings). While Performance Mode is locked, touch a knob to toggle its track's Looper — the knob LED is the track color when on.

#13.4 Presets

The step buttons are 16 preset slots, while Performance Mode is locked on or Loop is held:

  • Press one to recall it (again to turn it off); Shift + step saves; Delete + step clears.
  • Step LEDs: white = recalled, blue = saved, grey = empty.
  • Slots 1–8 ship with combinations (Float, Sink, Heartbeat, Fairy Dust, Robot, Dissolve, Chaos, Lift). You can save over them; they return to the factory set at the next launch.
  • Slots 9–16 are yours and are saved with the project.
Previous12. The ConductorNext14. Sound & Track Config
Chapter 14

Sound & Track Config

Each track's sound — its instrument, effects, levels, and the knobs that play them — is set in the track's own menu, TRACK CONFIG. Playback carries on and the pads and step buttons stay with the sequencer, so you can keep playing.

#14.1 Opening TRACK CONFIG

Open it from the CONFIG pad on the bank map (hold the jog, tap CONFIG, let go). The menu opens over the bank you were on; the jog moves its cursor and a click uses the row. Back from the top of the menu returns to that bank.

The track's levels are on MIX, the bottom pad of the CTRL column (Volume, Pan, Send A, Send B on knobs 1–4). On a MIDI track MIX holds that track's controllers instead — Expression, Pan, Mod, Sustain, Program, Bank MSB and Bank LSB. Touch Send A or Send B and click the jog to land in that send's effects (the knobs wear corner brackets to say so); Back returns to MIX. The session mixer does the same on its SEND A and SEND B pages: touch any track's knob and click.

#The channel strip

Turn the jog on MIX for its second page, MIX 2: the track's channel strip, like a mixing desk's channel. Turn the jog back for the levels.

KnobControlRange
1Low: a shelf at 100 Hz±15 dB
2Mid: a broad peak at the Mid Freq±15 dB
3Freq: where the Mid acts250 Hz – 5 kHz (about 1.1 kHz at the middle)
4High: a shelf at 10 kHz±15 dB
5Comp: a one-knob compressorOff – 100%
  • Each gain moves 0.5 dB a detent (Shift: 0.1 dB) and stops at 0 dB on its way across, like a desk's centre detent.
  • Comp is a desk-style compressor: one knob lowers the threshold, raises the ratio and adds make-up gain together. At 100% that is −30 dB, 4:1 and +7 dB. A dot on the knob shows how much it is turning the sound down right now.
  • Touch or turn an EQ knob to see the EQ curve over the page.
  • The comp comes first, then the EQ, then the track's fader and pan, so the sends hear it. A recording after the effects (Resample, Flatten) is taken before the strip, and the strip goes on working on the flattened track. Per-pad and module-bus sends are taken inside the instrument, before the strip.
  • The strip is saved with the project, can be automated, and is in track snapshots and SnapMorph. A flat strip with the comp off costs no CPU.
GestureResult
CONFIG pad on the bank mapOpen TRACK CONFIG
INST pad on the bank mapGo straight to the track's instrument
MIDI FX, INSTRUMENT, FX 1–4 pads on the bank map (the right-hand pads)Open that module's editor when you let go of the jog; Back returns you
BackStep out one level; from the top, back to the bank you were on
Hold BackReturn to the track overview; coming back brings the screen with it
Note/SessionClose it and go to Session View
  • Once open, the menu stays up until you leave it.
  • Outside a module's own pages, knobs 1–4 stay the track's levels.

Every list works as described in Menus & Project Settings.

  • Deeper screens open as overlays over the screen you came from, with a breadcrumb (T3 > Macros > Knobs).
  • A setting with more than two choices opens a list to pick from; backing out leaves it unchanged. The track's own settings at the foot of the menu are the exception: a click hands the setting to the jog.

#14.2 The menu

Video

Tutorial 1.6: Adding effects (from 6:14)

The rows run top to bottom in groups, with a line between them. A track shows only the rows it has:

RowWhat it does
MIDI FXA Schwung MIDI-effect module in front of the instrument (separate from the sequencer effects), so it sits above it — the rows follow the signal. On Move and MIDI tracks too: the track's notes go through it on their way to Move or the MIDI port.
Instmt/DestWhat the track plays — see Choosing an instrument. Click to edit it, Shift + click to change it. The menu opens on this row.
FX 1–4Four audio (insert) effects after it. Click an empty one to pick an effect. On a Move track these are the track's Move FX bus.
Volume, Pan, Send A, Send BThe track's levels. Shift + click a send to land in that send's own effects (or touch its knob on MIX and click); Back brings you home.
BusesVoice groups, on instruments that can split their voices — see Presets, LFOs and buses
PresetsSave and load the whole chain
LFOsTwo LFOs for the track
Mode, Transpose, VelIn, AftTch, Looper, Grv Amt, Export to MIDI, Flatten track, Parallel — and Grv Timing, Grv Velocity, Grv Random when the project uses a loaded grooveThe track's own settings — see Track settings

On the Instmt/Dest and effect rows, a hint band at the foot of the menu says what the click and the Shift chord do.

Swapping and reordering effects:

  • Shift + click an effect row to open its module list, with the loaded module in [brackets]. Pick another to swap it.
  • Indented under it, <Move up and >Move down swap the effect with its neighbour (each appears only toward a block that holds an effect). The effect keeps playing through the move — a reverb keeps its tail — and its automation, macros and preset name go with it.
  • The same rows reorder the Master, Send and Move FX buses.
  • Mute + click the jog on an effect row bypasses that effect without muting the track. Mute and solo live on the Mute button.

#14.3 Choosing an instrument

Video

Tutorial 1.5: Instruments (from 5:08)

Shift + click the Instmt/Dest row for the picker — one list, in groups:

GroupMakes the track
List: All(a filter, not an instrument — see below)
NoneA Schwung track with no instrument loaded — the state a new project's tracks 5–8 start in. Its MIDI FX, effects, levels and Presets stay, so you can load a chain preset straight away. On a Schwung track it removes the instrument.
Move 1–4Play one of Move's four instruments
ConductorA Conductor — converts the track behind a confirm, with the transport stopped
Every Schwung generator, by nameA Schwung track, with that instrument loaded
MIDI Ch 1–16A MIDI track: out the USB-A port on that channel
Track NPlay another track's instrument
  • A Move instrument belongs to one track at a time. One that another track already plays shows that track's number (Move 2 - T3) and the jog steps over it. To play it from a second track, point that track at the owner (Track N).
  • List: All (the top row) filters the generators to a list of your own. Click it to choose a list or make one (New List…, Rename, Delete, Clear); Shift + click a generator to add it to a list or take it out. Your Favorites wear a ★, in every list and in the effect browser.
  • If a change would leave macros or automation lanes with nothing to drive, dAVEBOx says how many and asks first (CHANGE TO …?).

To change a Move instrument's kit or preset, click the Instmt/Dest row — or tap INST on the bank map — to open Move's own editor for that instrument (Track View only), and work with it as you would on Move.

  • Move takes the screen, jog, knobs, Back, Mute and Shift (so Shift + jog works in Move's editor). Hold the jog and the bank map comes up over Move's screen — tap a bank or a track to leave for it, or let go to stay; a quick click is still Move's, landing as you let go; the pads, step buttons and transport stay with dAVEBOx, and dAVEBOx's own Shift gestures still work.
  • Press Back once you're at the top of Move's editor (the instrument's main screen) to come back, Note/Session to leave for Session View, or hold the jog and press Step 1–8 to leave and go straight to that track.

A plain click does nothing on a MIDI channel or a followed track. On a Schwung track with no instrument (or set to None), it opens the picker.

#14.4 Editing a module

Click an instrument or effect to open its editor: the knobs edit its parameters and the jog turns the pages. Shift + jog switches track, and the editor follows to the new track's instrument. A module that draws some of its own cells (a waveform, a picture of its mode) shows them in place of a plain dial.

The sequencer's page. Left / Right page the sequencer from the editor as they do on the track overview. While the transport runs, the bottom row shows the track's page bar in place of the hints: the page you're on solid, the page playing outlined, and the playhead. The hints come back when the transport stops. With the transport stopped, or on the TRACK CONFIG menu, each press shows SEQUENCER PAGE with the page number instead (2/4 = page 2 of a 4-page loop).

A module with its own screen. Some modules draw their own editor in Schwung instead of the standard pages. dAVEBOx shows that same screen, opened the same way: the knobs, the jog and the module's own gestures behave as they do in Schwung. If the module takes the pads (a drum module that jumps to the drum you hit, say), a pad goes to it first and still plays and records on the track. Its knobs record automation like any editor knob: hold a step and turn for a lock, or turn while recording. Back steps back inside the module, then leaves; Shift + jog leaves at once. Volume, Note/Session, Play and Record stay dAVEBOx's while it is up.

Touch a knob and click the jog for a parameter a knob can't turn well:

  • a file opens the file browser;
  • text opens the keyboard;
  • a long list opens a picker;
  • a sample marker opens a full-screen waveform (the jog moves the marker, knob 8 zooms, Shift + click picks the file).

The last two pages are the same for every module:

  • My Presets — the module's own presets. Preset opens the list, which auditions as you scroll; [Save current…] sits at its top, and Shift + click deletes one. Save As sits beside it; Save and Delete appear once one of your presets is loaded.
  • Module — Module Menu (the module's full parameter list, for settings the knob pages don't show), Module Help (when the module has it), Buses (when the instrument can split its voices — the same screen as the Sound menu's Buses row), Swap Module and Remove Module (the way to empty an effect slot). Swapping or removing asks first if macros or automation would be left behind.
    • On a MIDI effect the page also has Position (Post / Pre). See below.

Position — Pre or Post. Where a MIDI effect module sits, on any kind of track:

  • Post (the default): what you play is recorded as you played it, and the effect plays on top — on the clip and on your playing — on the way to the instrument. It comes first: the clip's notes go into the module, and the track's own clip effects (NOTE FX, Harmonize, MIDI Delay, SEQ ARP) work on what the module plays. So a MIDI Delay echoes an arpeggiator's notes, and Harmonize stacks on a chord module's chords. Note length (Gate, Len) is set before the module. On a drum track each of the module's notes plays on the lane whose note it is, with that lane's effects; a note no lane plays is not heard. Bake and Live Merge record the module's output into the clip and then bypass the module (it stays loaded, so you can undo or switch it back on), so the clip doesn't play through it twice.
  • Pre: what you play goes through the effect, and the effect's output is what you hear, what Record writes into the clip and what Capture keeps. The clip then plays back without the effect, so a chord effect records chords, an arpeggiator records its arpeggio, and nothing is played twice. On a drum track each note goes to the lane that plays it; notes no lane plays are heard but not recorded.
  • Pads and an external keyboard both go through it.
  • The setting is saved with the project and goes back to Post when the effect is removed. An effect that used Notes to Seq switches to Pre the first time you open it.

How the knobs feel — in a module's editor, on MACROS, and for pan and the sends on MIX and in the session mixer:

  • Every knob sweeps its whole range in the same gesture; turning faster moves further.
  • A count or a list — voices, a pad number, a transpose, anything up to about 48 values — takes four clicks per step.
  • An On/Off or two-choice knob goes On (or to its second choice) turning right and Off turning left, and doesn't wrap.
  • Hold Shift for fine control — a tenth of the step, or one option per click on a list.

Drum modules follow the pad you hit: playing a pad brings that drum's parameters up on screen. Only a pad you physically press counts — a playing pattern or incoming MIDI never moves the editor.

#14.5 Presets, LFOs and buses

Presets (the SLOT PRESETS screen) saves and loads the track's whole chain — instrument, effects and macros:

  • [Save] overwrites the loaded preset (it asks first); [Save as…] names a new one.
  • Click a preset to load it; Shift + click deletes it.
  • A * marks the loaded preset.

LFOs opens LFO 1 and LFO 2, on Schwung and Move tracks:

SettingRange
TargetAny parameter of the track's modules, or the other LFO's Depth, Rate or Phase
EnabledOn, Off
ShapeSine, Tri, Saw, Square, S&H, Swishy
ModeUnipolar, Bipolar
SyncFree, Sync
Rate0.1–20 Hz free, or 16 bars to 1/32T synced
Depth−1 to 1
PhaseStart point of the wave
RetriggerRestart the wave with each note

Buses appears below Send B only on an instrument that can split its voices, such as a drum module (and on the instrument editor's Module page). It lists the instrument's buses and New Bus. Each bus has:

  • Voices — which voices play through it. Play a pad and the list jumps to that voice; click to take it. A voice belongs to one bus at a time.
  • its own Inserts, and Send A and Send B levels;
  • Rename and Delete.

#14.6 The MACROS bank

Video

Tutorial 5.4: Macros (from 3:58)

MACROS is the top pad of the CTRL column on the bank map, with AUTO below it. Its eight knobs play whatever you assign to them, and each cell shows its target's value the way the module editor does — a dial, a big number, a list square, a fader for a level. A knob with no target, or whose target was swapped away, shows -- and reads UNASSIGNED when touched.

Touch a knob and click the jog to edit that macro. Every macro's cell has corner brackets; while you touch one, the bottom of the screen reads CLK ASSIGN (nothing assigned yet) or CLK EDIT.

  • On an unassigned knob, choose a module (or a bank, Levels, MIDI, or SnapMorph), then a parameter, and you're back on the MACROS page.
  • On an Audio or Slicer track the list also has Sample (SAMPLE's Gain, Pitch, Detune and Tempo) and, on a Slicer, All Slices (the every-slice settings Shift shows on the SLICER editor). The knob turns the clip the track is on, as the editor's own knob would, and records the same lane. Of the banks it offers only CLIP and NOTE FX.
  • (None) at the top clears the knob.
  • If the same module sits in two slots, the slot is shown beside its name.

#One knob, several parameters

Once a knob has a target, touch + click opens it — a short list of everything the knob drives, each entry with its Lo, Hi and Travel:

Ctff          Syn>cutoff
  Lo                  0%
  Hi                100%
  Travel         Bounded
+ Add target
  • + Add target puts another parameter on the same knob, each with its own range.
  • Click an entry to point it somewhere else (it keeps its range); Shift + click removes it.
  • Lo and Hi set how far the parameter travels as the knob goes from bottom to top. Set Hi below Lo and it runs backwards, so one knob can open a filter while it closes a reverb. On a list parameter they choose a span of the list. You hear a range as you set it. A module parameter's range is a percentage; a dAVEBOx bank knob's or an Audio clip setting's is in its own units (Tempo in BPM, 1 BPM a detent, Shift for 0.1). A new Tempo target starts with Hi at 400 BPM; raise it here if you need more. With a range set, the knob's dial runs from Lo to Hi.
  • Travel — Bounded (the default) keeps the parameter's own feel and stops at the range; Full spreads the range across the knob's whole sweep. Full suits a filter, not a parameter with only a few values. On a dAVEBOx bank knob or an Audio clip's setting, Bounded steps as finely as the range is narrow: Tempo held to 120–140 BPM moves 0.1 BPM a detent.

A knob on a single target behaves like that target: its own dial, its own steps. A knob on several targets shows its own position as a percentage under a short name (MAC1, MAC2…, numbered in knob order); touch it and the header says what it drives (CTFF +2).

Recording: a macro records as its parameters.

  • Turn it while recording and each parameter records its own lane; turn it while holding a step and that step takes a lock.
  • Delete + touch clears all its lanes at once; Mute + touch switches them off together.
  • A parameter recorded separately is pulled back in line by the next turn of the macro.
  • A macro on a LIVE ARP setting moves it but is never recorded.

MIDI targets. Any track can point a macro at Aftertouch or Pitch Bend (pick MIDI); a MIDI track can also point one at any MIDI CC (pick MIDI CC, then the number). Pitch bend springs back to centre when you let go; Shift + turn latches it.

Assignments belong to the project, and a saved chain preset carries them with it.

#14.7 Sound snapshots & SnapMorph

Video

Tutorial 5.5: Sound snapshots and SnapMorph (from 6:12)

Hold Capture and the 16 step buttons become sound snapshots. In Track View they hold the active track's sound; in Session View, the whole device's.

Gesture (Capture held)Result
Shift + stepSave the sound into that slot
StepRecall it
Delete + stepClear the slot

Undo takes back a recall. A snapshot holds every module's settings, the effect buses, the mixer levels and the macro positions — not mutes.

SnapMorph turns one knob into a path between two or more of the track's snapshots. Touch an unassigned macro, click, and pick SnapMorph (the last entry), then click the snapshot slots in the order the knob should travel: [1] at the bottom of the turn, [2] next, and so on. The knob is live as soon as two are in.

  • Numbers the snapshots share glide (volume moves in dB, the way the fader travels); a choice — a waveform, a switch — flips halfway across.
  • A block whose module differs between the snapshots stays out of the morph.
  • On a Move track the morph covers the track's bus effects and levels; a MIDI track has nothing to morph.
  • The knob shows its position under MORPH; Lo and Hi window the path.
  • It records as one lane (SnapMorph K4 on the AUTOMATION screen) and doesn't export to Live.

#14.8 Master FX and the sends

Video

Tutorial 6.1: The session mixer and the sends

Three buses sit across every track — MASTER FX and the two sends, SEND FX A and SEND FX B — each with four effect blocks, edited exactly like a track's.

  • Master FX processes everything on its way out.
  • A send is fed by each track's Send A or Send B level, so several tracks can share one reverb or delay. Each send's Return level sets how much comes back into the mix.

To reach them, hold the jog in Session View, tap MASTER, SEND A or SEND B on the Session map and let go. Back from an effect bus's top level returns to the Session overview.

Previous13. Performance ModeNext15. Routing & Sync
Chapter 15

Routing & Sync

#15.1 Instruments & routing

A track's destination is its Instmt/Dest row, at the top of TRACK CONFIG: one of Move 1–4, a Schwung generator, a MIDI channel (out USB-A), another track's instrument, or None (a Schwung track with nothing loaded).

  • A new project starts with tracks 1–4 on Move 1–4 and tracks 5–8 on Schwung.
  • Several tracks can go to MIDI channels at once for a multitimbral rig.
  • Tracks that play Move instruments need Link enabled in Move's System Settings; dAVEBOx warns you (LINK AUDIO ROUTE) if it's off.

#15.2 External MIDI in and out

A USB-A controller plays the active track, its notes moved onto that track's channel; filter by channel with MIDI In in Project Settings. On a drum track an incoming note plays the lane set to that note. What shapes live input depends on where the track goes:

DestinationLive external input
SchwungThrough the sequencer effects
MIDI channelThrough the sequencer effects, out USB-A
Another trackThrough the sequencer effects, into that track's instrument
MoveStraight to Move, without the sequencer effects (they would loop back). With a MIDI FX module loaded, notes go through the module first

On a track set to a MIDI channel, everything goes out USB-A — the sequence, live pads, effects and automation. Transport Stop sends note-offs; Delete + Play while stopped sends a MIDI panic on every channel.

Bluetooth MIDI. On a Move with a Bluetooth radio, a paired Bluetooth LE MIDI device works like one plugged into USB-A: it plays the active track, and it receives everything sent out USB-A. Bluetooth in Project Settings turns the radio on or off. SysEx is not carried.

#15.3 Clock Follow

dAVEBOx runs its own clock by default. Set Clock Follow → Move in Project Settings to lock to Move's transport instead: dAVEBOx sequences while Move supplies clock, transport and voices.

  • Tempo comes from Move. BPM shows Move and can't be changed; Tap Tempo says Tempo follows Move.
  • Play drives Move. dAVEBOx's Play starts and stops Move's transport, and both launch from the same downbeat.
  • Recording starts Move and counts one bar on its clock before it records.
  • If Move's clock stops, so does dAVEBOx — though held arpeggios and synced delay keep running at Move's tempo. If Move doesn't start, dAVEBOx plays on at its last tempo and shows CLOCK FOLLOW / Move didn't start.
  • Keep Move's own sequencer empty on the tracks dAVEBOx feeds.

Leave Clock Follow Off for the normal internal clock.

#15.4 Clock Out

Clock Out → On sends MIDI clock and start/stop out the USB-A port, so external gear locks to dAVEBOx. It applies while free-running; with Clock Follow on Move it is suppressed and shows —.

Previous14. Sound & Track ConfigNext16. Bake, Merge & Export
Chapter 16

Bake, Merge & Export

Tap Sample for a short menu of what it can do — turn the jog to choose, press it to go, and Back steps back a level:

  • Session View: Bake scene, Resample scene, Resample clip, Live merge.
  • Track View: Bake clip, Resample clip, Live merge track.

Bake scene and Resample scene then ask for the row: tap a side button, or a step button for any of the 16. Resample clip in Session View asks for the clip: tap its pad. In Track View it takes the track's current clip.

#16.1 Bake

Video

Tutorial 4.6: Bake (from 8:01)

Bake renders a clip's sequencer effects — NOTE FX, HARMONY, DELAY, SEQ ARP — into plain notes, then resets those effects. The clip sounds the same, with a clean effects chain to build on.

  • An Audio clip has no notes to bake: Bake clip records what the clip plays — its REMIX and all — into a new sample in its place (BAKE CLIP: a resample In place, §16.6), and the clip starts over with it.
  • A Slicer clip bakes its REMIX first: the remixed steps — their reversals and pitches written onto each step's own sound — become the clip's, then NOTE FX bakes over them. The slices themselves are never changed, so the Slicer's other clips sound the same.
  • A melodic clip (Track View): Sample → Bake clip, then choose the loop count (1× / 2× / 4×) and whether to wrap the delay tails for a seamless loop.
  • A drum clip adds a first choice — the whole clip, or just the selected lane.
  • A scene (Session View): Sample → Bake scene, choose the row, then make the same choices. Empty clips are skipped.
  • When you bake a scene whose Conductor clip has responding tracks, a last Apply Conductor? step can fold its transposition into those clips. Baking a single clip never applies the Conductor. An Audio clip's slices never move: when the Conductor holds one shift wherever the clip hears it, the shift goes into the clip's Pitch and the track stops following; when it changes, the clip is left alone and the track keeps following the Conductor live (the notice names it).
  • A MIDI effect module in play. When the clip's track has a MIDI effect module set to Post (loaded and not bypassed), Bake runs the module too: pick the loop count, and in a moment (BAKING) the clip holds what you would hear — the module's notes with dAVEBOx's effects on them. It works with the transport running or stopped; nothing is played. The module is then bypassed (not removed), so the clip isn't processed twice; Undo puts the clip back. Back cancels and leaves the clip as it was. A Pre module is already in the clip, so it bakes instantly as usual.
    • Shift held on the confirm prints it live instead: with the transport stopped, the clip plays alone after a one-bar count-in (PRINTING) and what you hear becomes the clip. Use it if a module bakes differently from how it plays (BAKE FAILED suggests it too).
    • On a drum clip each of the module's hits lands on the lane whose note it is, with that lane's effects; a hit no lane plays is dropped.
  • Scene bakes and Export to Live stay instant and leave a Post MIDI effect module out; they tell you which tracks.

#16.2 Live Merge

Live Merge records the actual output of your tracks — arps, delays, knob rides and all — into plain clips.

  • Arm it from a stopped transport with Sample → Live merge (in Track View, Live merge track); a notice says what it will capture and Press Rec to start.
  • Press Record to begin: a 1-bar count-in, then a clean take from the top. Back cancels at any point, even at the placing step.
  • The view you arm from sets the scope:
    • Session View — all 8 tracks, committed to a scene row you pick.
    • Track View — the active track alone; when you stop, Session View opens with that track's empty clips blinking. Tap one to keep the take.
  • Press Record again to stop (or it stops at the 256-step limit), then tap a destination to place the take.
  • Audio tracks record their sound, not the slices they trigger: everything the track plays, pads included, before its effects. Each Audio track gets its own recording, and it goes into that track's clip at the destination as a Loop sample, so it still plays through the track's effects. An Audio track that made no sound keeps its clip. With an Audio track in the merge, Record stops at the end of the bar, so the recording loops.

#16.3 Export to Live

Project Settings → Export to Ableton (transport stopped) writes an .ablbundle that desktop Live opens directly. The screen shows where it was saved: download it from the Files page of the Schwung web manager (move.local:7700), in the daveboxSA/davebox-exports folder. It opens as 8 tracks × 16 scene slots with the tempo and root note (not the scale — the set opens in Major).

  • Move tracks export the real Move instrument and preset. Every track keeps its dAVEBOx color.
  • Schwung, MIDI and Conductor tracks get a placeholder (so does a Move track with no matching Move instrument), switched off: the notes are there, but nothing plays until you drop in your own instrument.
  • Audio tracks become Live audio tracks, each clip recorded as it sounds. Before it writes the bundle, export plays every Audio clip once to warm up, then records it: through the track's effects, at its level and pan, with its automation, and with the Conductor when you answer Yes to Apply Conductor?. A muted or soloed-out track is recorded too. Each recording is exactly as long as the clip loops (up to 256 bars, or where it and the Conductor's clip line up), so it loops in Live as it does here. Most clips are rendered much faster than they play, and the card counts up a percentage. A clip whose sound can't be copied is recorded in real time instead, with the same result, and the card says why: Modulation, Line input, A macro lane and so on. Back while it records cancels the export. Your project isn't changed. Sends come across as for any track, but the recordings don't include the Master FX.
  • Schwung tracks are named for what they played — SCH-nusaw, or SCH-nusaw - Big Lead when the module reports a patch name (most modules don't).
  • Send levels come across, along with two empty return tracks to send to. Level and pan come across as automation.
  • A track's channel strip comes across as Live devices: a Compressor with the same threshold, ratio and make-up, then a Channel EQ. Live's Channel EQ has its own fixed shelves and a Mid of ±12 dB at most, so the EQ is an approximation, and the screen says which tracks (EQ/Comp approx). Automation of the strip doesn't come across. An Audio track's strip is already in its recording.
  • Notes are baked — each clip exports what you hear: effects rendered, delay tails wrapped, drum polymeters flattened, and randomized clips written as several loops of variation.
  • A remix exports as you hear it: an Audio or Slicer clip with REMIX on is rendered with it (Live has no remix of its own), and a Slicer's steps play their own Pitch, Length, Start and Dir.
  • An Apply Conductor? step works as it does for bake, and never changes your live set.
  • Automation comes too — see below.

The bundle carries its own samples. Move Drum Racks need Live 12.1+. Export is one-way.

#What automation carries

Carried:

  • Volume, pan and both sends, as clip automation on the track's mixer.
  • Aftertouch on any track.
  • Pitch bend on Move-routed tracks, scaled to that instrument's own bend range.

Aftertouch and pitch bend are written onto the notes rather than as a separate lane, so they exist only while a note is sounding.

Each lane has the same shape in Live as it plays here: it glides and jumps where it does here, and a Wrap: Reset lane holds its last value to the end of its loop and drops straight back to its start. Points left outside a lane's loop (after the loop was shortened) don't play here, so they aren't exported.

Not carried:

  • CC automation — a Move set has no place for a CC curve.
  • SnapMorph lanes — a morph knob has no Live equivalent, and the parameters it drove aren't exported either.
  • Pitch bend on Schwung tracks — the bend range is set by the synth, and a Schwung track exports as a placeholder.
  • Audio tracks' automation, as lanes: it is in each clip's recording, and only the sends come across as automation.
  • Automation inside a Schwung module, and dAVEBOx's own bank parameters — neither exists in Live.
  • The part of a lane that runs past its clip. A lane can be longer than its clip in dAVEBOx — a 4-bar filter sweep over a 1-bar loop — but in Live a clip's automation loops with the clip, so the export keeps only the stretch inside the clip and repeats it.

#16.4 Import a MIDI file

Video

Tutorial 7.2: MIDI import and export (from 1:01)

Touch knob 8 on the CLIP or DRUM LANE bank and click the jog (any track except a Conductor, whatever it plays through). The MIDI browser fills the clip you are on from a standard MIDI file (.mid, .midi, .smf, .kar, .rmi). Keep your MIDI files anywhere in your user data folder — the Files page of the Schwung web manager (move.local:7700) uploads there. Your own exports are in the daveboxSA folder, which shows only its MIDI folder. The notes are copied into the clip; the file isn't needed afterwards. No MIDI files come with dAVEBOx.

It has three layers, and Back steps out of one at a time:

The list. On a track's first visit the browser opens on your user data folder. Turn the jog to move through it; every file plays as you land on it, in place of what the track plays: in time with the song while the track is playing, otherwise on its own. Each file shows its length in bars (and DRM if it is all drums). Click a folder (NAME/) to go in; .. at the top goes up. A file with several parts (a song with a lead, a bass line and drums) shows NAME> and its part count: click it to go in, and its parts are laid out like files. A name too long for its row scrolls while the cursor is on it, so you can read all of it. Click a file (or part) to pick it — the card comes up. Back goes up a level, as .. does; at the top it leaves the browser (asking first, as the card's Back does, if you had picked a file). Hold Back to leave from anywhere.

The card is the file you picked, still playing. Its knobs work like a bank's: touching one names it, and turning Stretch (or, on a drum track, Map) brings up its list.

  • Knob 1, Start — the bar of the file to start from.
  • Knob 2, Bars — how many bars land in the clip. Never more than the file has from Start, nor than the clip holds at this resolution: 1/16 holds 16 bars of 4/4.
  • Knob 3, Res — the clip's resolution (its step size), 1/32 to a whole bar, as on the CLIP bank. It doesn't move the notes: each keeps its timing.
  • Knob 4, Stretch — play it at /8, /4, /2, x1, x2, x4 or x8 of its length.
  • Knob 5, Oct and knob 6, Semi — move it up or down (three octaves, or eleven semitones).
  • Knob 7, Scale — On folds every note into your project's key and scale (a note between two scale notes goes up); Off plays it as written. Oct and Semi move the notes first, so they set where the fold lands.
  • Knob 8 shows the file's tempo (BPM), if it has one.

Each new file starts at Start 1, Res 1/16, Stretch x1 and its own length.

On a drum track, knob 5 is Map instead: where the file's drum sounds go — GM (the lanes playing their General MIDI notes), Move (Move's own kit layout) or Off (from the lane you are on). The right-hand pads are the file's sounds, each in its colour: hold one to hear it alone and see where every sound goes, and tap a lane pad to put it there (again to take it off). Up to eight sounds are placed.

The line under the top knobs is the file's notes: the brackets are what will land, notes outside them are dotted, and a playhead follows the preview. The top right says what won't land — CUT (outside the brackets), OVER (past the clip's note limit), OFF (drum sounds with no lane) — or REPLACES when the clip already has notes. Shift + jog click mutes and unmutes the preview (the notes on the line blink while it is muted). The jog brings the list back.

Loading asks first. Jog click on the card: LOAD INTO CLIP A? — turn the jog to Yes and click. It goes into the clip you are on and replaces it — on a drum track, only the lanes a sound goes to; the other lanes keep their notes. One Undo takes the whole load back. Back from the card with a file picked asks whether to load it first: Yes loads and leaves, No (or Back) leaves without loading. Either way you are back on the CLIP or DRUM LANE bank.

Each track remembers its own last file while you work, so a drum track and a melodic track can each come back to their own folder.

  • Only notes come in — no controllers, pitch bend or program changes.
  • A melodic clip's automation is cleared with it, so it plays exactly the file's notes (Undo brings it back with the rest).
  • The file's tempo isn't applied: the notes play at your project's tempo, and bars follow the file's time signature.
  • A melodic clip holds up to 512 notes; a drum lane, 512.
  • The transport keeps running while you browse; the step buttons are blocked (lit dim).

#16.5 Export a clip as a MIDI file

Video

Tutorial 7.2: MIDI import and export (from 1:01)

Open the track's TRACK CONFIG menu, turn to Export to MIDI and click. The clip you are on is saved as a standard MIDI file, as it plays: NOTE FX, harmony, the arp and the delay are baked in, a clip with random settings is saved as 8 cycles, and a track that follows the Conductor is saved transposed. A drum clip is one file, each lane on its own note (channel 10). A MIDI effect module set to Post is left out — Bake the clip first to keep it.

The file goes to the MIDI folder inside dAVEBOx SA's own folder (daveboxSA/MIDI), named after the project, track and clip (mngk 3B.mid); a second export of the same clip adds 2 rather than overwriting. Download it from the Files page of the Schwung web manager (the dAVEBOx MIDI link at the top), or bring it back with Import MIDI. Stop the transport first — like the Ableton export, it won't run while playing.

#16.6 Recording audio

Resample a scene to record what it sounds like into a sample, cut to loop exactly:

  • With the transport stopped (and Clock Follow off), Sample → Resample scene, then choose the row.
  • Length starts where all the scene's clips line up again (past 32 bars, the longest clip); turn the jog to change it. Warm-up plays the scene once first, so delay and reverb tails carry into the start of the loop. Tail records extra bars after the clips stop, for the ring-out — the file is then longer than the loop. Both start off.
  • Press the jog on Start: the scene plays from the top with no count-in and the metronome silent, and RESAMPLING counts the bars. RESAMPLED says what it recorded when it is done. As with a MIDI FX print, Back cancels and the other buttons wait until it's done.
  • It records the whole mix, after Master FX. Files go to the sample library under Samples → dAVEBOx → Resample, named after the project, scene, length and tempo (mngk Scene C 4bar 120bpm.wav), where Move's own sampler can use them. They are not part of the project.

Resample a clip the same way: Sample → Resample clip. Only that track plays while it records. Its options add Source: Wet is the track as you hear it, with its send effects and Master FX; Dry is just the track's own instrument and effects at its level — for a Move instrument, its Move track through its FX 1–4. Warm-up starts on for a Move instrument, because it sounds a few milliseconds late. The file is named like an exported clip (mngk 3B 2bar 120bpm.wav). A muted track, or one that plays MIDI out, has nothing to record.

Audio and Slicer tracks resample like any other. An Audio clip plays its sample with no steps, so its length is the clip's own; a Slicer clip's is its sequence's. An Audio clip's options add In place: turned on, the recording goes into the project instead of the library and replaces the clip. The clip starts over with the recording as its sample, at default settings. (A Slicer has no In place: its sample is the whole track's.) It's recorded before the track's effects and volume, which go on playing on it, so they apply once; Source shows -.

Flatten a track to turn it into audio: open its TRACK CONFIG menu, turn to Flatten track and click. With the transport stopped (and Clock Follow off), every clip with notes is recorded on its own, one after another, and the track becomes an Audio track with each clip playing its recording (a Slicer becomes an Audio track the same way). The notes and the instrument go. Its options come first; press the jog on Flatten to start:

  • Effects: Pre (the default) records the instrument before the track's effects, which stay on the Audio track and keep sounding — you can still change them. Post records through the effects, then bypasses them so they don't apply twice. They stay in place, so you can switch them back on. Either way the recording leaves out the track's volume and pan (the Audio track still has them) and its sends. A Move instrument's effects are the ones on its FX 1–4: they're copied onto the Audio track, with the Move track's volume, pan and sends, and the originals stay where they were. The same goes for a track that plays another track's instrument.
  • Warm-up plays each clip once before recording it, so delay and reverb tails carry into the start of the loop. It starts on for a Move instrument (which sounds a few milliseconds late), off otherwise.
  • Back changes nothing; Back while it records cancels the whole flatten.

Drum tracks flatten too, and so does a MIDI track that plays another track's instrument (it records that instrument with this track's notes). An Audio track flattens in place: every clip with a sample is recorded and starts over with its recording, at default settings, as In place does for one clip. A track that plays MIDI out, has no instrument, is muted or has no notes (or samples) has nothing to flatten.

Undo right after a flatten brings the track back as it was: its notes (or drum clips), its type, its instrument with its own sound, its routing, and its effects and levels as they were (switched back on if Post bypassed them). Shift + Undo flattens it again. Choosing Audio in Instmt/Dest comes back the same way. As with any Undo, only the last change can be undone.

Faster than real time. A Flatten, or a Resample clip In place, of a track that plays a Schwung instrument, or of an Audio track, records without playing: the clips aren't heard, and each one takes a fraction of its length — Dry takes too, and the track's MIDI effects and the automation the take can hear come along. It records in real time instead, as before, when the sound can't be copied: a modulation source (an LFO) on it, an effect that listens to MIDI, voices sent to buses, the line input, a knob mapped to a controller the clip sends, the track's own macro lane, automation of a MIDI effect, or a MIDI effect that plays into the sequencer. Move instruments and Wet takes always record in real time. When it does, the card says why (Real time: Modulation), so you know what to change to make it fast.

After any resample, the clips you had armed are armed again, so Play carries on from where you were.

For anything else, use Schwung's two samplers — both work inside dAVEBOx:

  • Quantized Sampler — hold Shift, touch the Volume knob and press Sample.
  • Skipback — hold Shift, touch the Volume knob and press Capture. Its length is set under Host Settings... → Audio → Skipback Len.

Settings & Projects

#The groove

Video

Tutorial 6.4: Groove and swing (from 7:23)

One groove plays for the whole project. Groove picks it and Groove Amt says how much of it you hear — at none, everything is on the grid.

  • Swing 1/16 and Swing 1/8 delay every other 1/16 or 1/8. These are the Swing Amt and Swing Res of earlier versions, and a project made with them opens sounding the same.
  • Browse... opens a file list showing MIDI files and Ableton groove files (.agr). Rest the jog on one and you hear it at once, over whatever is playing; click to keep it and return to Project Settings. Back leaves without keeping anything — the groove you had comes back. The list opens on the file the project's groove was loaded from, or at the top of your files when the project has none. A MIDI file is read over its whole length, on the grid its notes were played on — 1/16s for a 1/16 pattern, 1/8s for swung 1/8s, triplets for triplets — up to 128 positions; a file with several parts asks which. An Ableton groove brings its own grid, length and amounts.
  • A loaded groove is a pattern of small timing shifts — some notes a little late, some a little early — and velocities, one per grid position, that repeats. Notes the sequencer plays are moved both ways; arps, repeats, delay echoes and the looper are only ever moved later. It appears at the foot of the list under its name, so you can go to a swing and come back.
  • Off plays straight whatever Groove Amt says.

The groove you load is saved inside the project, so the project keeps its feel even if the file is later removed.

Each track follows the project's amounts until you give it its own. In a track's settings, Grv Amt reads Global; turn it and that track takes its own amount instead — more than the rest, less, or 0 % to play straight. With a loaded groove, Grv Timing, Grv Velocity and Grv Random work the same way, so a hi-hat can wander while the kick stays put, or one track can take the groove's accents and another ignore them. Turn a row back down to Global and the track follows again.

Recording under a groove: with Input Quantize off, what you play is stored so that the groove plays it back at the moment you played it — it is not grooved a second time. With Input Quantize on, the note snaps to the grid and the groove moves it from there.

  • The menu groups these with a line between each group, in this order.
  • The header shows the battery at the right: its charge in percent, with a plug in place of the battery while the Move is on the charger. Move reports the level only when it changes by 1 %, so just after launch it shows the last level dAVEBOx saw.
  • When Move says the battery is low (around 6 %) and it is not on the charger, a LOW BATTERY card comes up over whatever screen you are on. Click the jog to dismiss it; the click does nothing else, and nothing below takes a press while the card is up (the music keeps playing). It comes back every 5 minutes until you plug the Move in.
  • A new project starts in a random key and scale.
  • Card Hold, Bluetooth, Host Settings... and Move Settings... apply to every project, not just this one.
  • Move Settings... shows Move's own settings menu on the screen: turn the jog to choose, click to open or change, Back to step out. The pads, steps, knobs and transport stay dAVEBOx's, so the music plays on. Shift + Step 2 or Back at the top of Move's menu brings you back here; Note/Session goes to Session View.
  • Tap Tempo is Shift + Step 5: tap any pad in time, or turn the jog to adjust; click or Back when done.

Scales: Major, Minor, Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, Mixolydian, Locrian, Harmonic Minor, Melodic Minor, Pentatonic Major, Pentatonic Minor, Blues, Whole Tone, Diminished.

#17.2 Key & Scale

Editing Key or Scale moves your melodic clips with it:

  • Click Key or Scale to open the list, turn to choose, and click to pick.
  • If any melodic clip holds notes, TRANSPOSE CLIPS? asks first: Yes moves the notes to the new key; No keeps the old key. Back cancels too. While it asks, the pads show the new key and, while playing, you hear the clips in it. With no notes to move, the pick commits straight away.
  • Key moves by the shortest distance. Scale remaps by scale degree between scales of the same size, otherwise to the nearest in-scale note.
  • Drum tracks are untouched.
  • A committed transpose can't be undone — check the preview before you confirm.
  • Instruments and MIDI effects that can follow the host's key (a Host setting) follow dAVEBOx's key, scale and tempo, live — the preview too.

#17.3 Snapshots

dAVEBOx saves as you go (Saving). For named backups, Save state keeps up to 16 snapshots per project:

  • Each is stamped with the date and time. Saving asks first; when all 16 are used, it asks which one to replace.
  • Load state restores one.
  • Snapshots belong to the project and survive Clear Sess.
  • Snapshots saved by a different dAVEBOx version can't be loaded; Load state offers to delete them.

Every kind of preset and snapshot at a glance:

KindHoldsKeptRecall
Save state (above)The whole projectWith the project, 16Project Settings → Load state
Sound snapshotsA track's sound (Track View) or every track's (Session View)With the project, 16Hold Capture, tap a step
Mute snapshotsMute and solo statesWith the project, 16Session View: Mute + step
Performance presetsA combination of Performance modsWith the project (1–8 are factory)Performance Mode: a step
Chain presetsA track's whole chain — instrument, effects, macrosOn the device, for every projectTRACK CONFIG → Presets
Module presetsOne instrument's or effect's settingsOn the device, for every projectThe module's My Presets page

#17.4 Track settings

These sit in the track's TRACK CONFIG menu, in short groups below the sound rows — not in Project Settings. Click a row to give it the jog, turn to change the value, then click (or Back) to let go. Rows that don't apply to the track's type or route are hidden, so the list is shorter on a MIDI track or a Conductor.
